artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers in a Glass Vase
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, copper (metal), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 6.8 cm × height 54.5 cm x width 36.5 cm
artworks.description: De Utrechtenaar Jan Davidsz de Heem verhuisde in 1636 naar Antwerpen. Daar specialiseerde hij zich onder invloed van de Vlaamse meesters in het schilderen van pronkstillevens en festoenen. Hoewel de aandacht voor detail herinnert aan zijn Utrechtse leermeester Balthasar van der Ast, is de zwier en de rijkdom aan kleur eerder Vlaams.

artworks.title: The Milkmaid
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 45.5 cm x width 41 cm
artworks.description: A maidservant pours milk, entirely absorbed in her work. Except for the stream of milk, everything else is still. Vermeer took this simple everyday activity and made it the subject of an impressive painting – the woman stands like a statue in the brightly lit room. Vermeer also had an eye for how light by means of hundreds of colourful dots plays over the surface of objects.

artworks.title: The Night Watch Militia Company of District II under the Command of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 379.5 cm x width 453.5 cm x weight 337 kg x weight 170 kg
artworks.description: Rembrandt’s largest, most famous canvas was made for the Arquebusiers guild hall. This was one of several halls of Amsterdam’s civic guard, the city’s militia and police. Rembrandt was the first to paint figures in a group portrait actually doing something. The captain, dressed in black, is telling his lieutenant to start the company marching. The guardsmen are getting into formation. Rembrandt used the light to focus on particular details, like the captain’s gesturing hand and the young girl in the background. She was the company mascot.

artworks.title: Children of the Sea
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 48.5 cm x width 93.5 cm x height 49 cm x width 91 cm
artworks.description: This charming scene contains a message. The children of a fisherman, with their tattered rags and paltry toys, offer us a glimpse of their future. The eldest boy carries the weight of the family on his shoulders, and the little boat stands for the rigours of life at sea. Jozef Israëls first painted this subject in 1863. It became enormously popular and the artist subsequently repeated it often.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers and a Watch
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 8 cm × height 75 cm x width 60 cm
artworks.description: De bloemen in dit weelderige boeket zijn zorgvuldig gerangschikt op vorm en kleur. Het licht dat subtiel langs de bloemen strijkt laat het boeket scherp afsteken tegen de donkere achtergrond. Naast het boeket ligt een opengeklapt zakhorloge met een blauw lintje eraan. Dit uurwerk en de over de bloemen kruipende insecten wijzen op de vergankelijkheid van het bestaan – de tijd die langzaam verstrijkt en alles aantast.

artworks.title: View of Houses in Delft, Known as ‘The Little Street’
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 54.3 cm x width 44 cm x depth 9 cm
artworks.description: This is an unusual painting in Vermeer’s oeuvre, and remarkable for its time as a portrait of ordinary houses. The composition is as exciting as it is balanced. The old walls with their bricks, whitewash, and cracks are almost tangible. The location is Vlamingstraat 40–42  in Delft. Vermeer’s aunt Ariaentgen Claes lived in the house at the right, with her children, from around 1645 until her death in 1670.

artworks.title: Winter Landscape with Ice Skaters
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 77.3 cm x width 131.9 cm
artworks.description: The high vantage point of this painting turns it into a sampler of human – and animal – activity during a harsh winter. Hundreds of people are out on the ice, most of them for pleasure, others working out of dire necessity. Avercamp did not shy away from grim details: in the left foreground crows and a dog feast on the carcass of a horse that has frozen to death.

artworks.title: Floral Still Life
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 67.6 cm x width 53.3 cm × outer size: depth 6 cm (support incl. frame)
artworks.description: This exuberant bouquet may look natural, but tulips, anemones, roses and carnations do not all bloom at the same time. Bollongier nevertheless managed to assemble a balanced composition. The still life was painted shortly after the Dutch stock market crashed in 1637, when many people went bankrupt due to the speculation in tulip bulbs. This festive bouquet may thus refer to the transience of earthly matters.

artworks.title: The Threatened Swan
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 144 cm x width 171 cm
artworks.description: A swan fiercely defends its nest against a dog. In later centuries this scuffle was interpreted as a political allegory: the white swan was thought to symbolize the Dutch statesman Johan de Witt (assassinated in 1672) protecting the country from its enemies. This was the meaning attached to the painting when it became the very first acquisition to enter the Nationale Kunstgalerij (the forerunner of the Rijksmuseum) in 1800.

artworks.title: Girl in a White Kimono
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 59 cm x width 57 cm x depth 11 cm
artworks.description: The model for this painting was called Geesje Kwak, then a sixteen-year-old housemaid from Amsterdam. She is dressed in a Japanese kimono, a popular subject for Breitner. He made thirteen paintings of girls in kimonos, inspired by Japanese prints, which he as well collected. However, for Europeans, wearing Asian clothing since long also had a sexual inference.

artworks.title: Self-portrait
artworks.medium: paper, paint (coating), pasteboard, cardboard, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 42 cm x width 34 cm × depth 8 cm
artworks.description: Vincent moved to Paris in 1886, after hearing from his brother Theo about the new, colourful style of French painting. Wasting no time, he tried it out in several self-portraits. He did this mostly to avoid having to pay for a model. Using rhythmic brushstrokes in striking colours, he portrayed himself here as a fashionably dressed Parisian.

artworks.title: Italian Landscape with Umbrella Pines
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 101.5 cm x width 138.5 cm
artworks.description: Voogd was known as the ‘Dutch Claude’, after the French painter Claude Lorrain, who was famous for his history landscapes bathed in golden light. Voogd painted the gardens of the Villa Borghese in Rome in the late afternoon. The sun casts long shadows, and the trees stand out sharply against the sky. Strolling figures are enjoying the magnificent sunset. In the foreground, an artist is seated against a tree and drawing.

artworks.title: Woman Reading a Letter
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 70 cm x width 63 cm × height 46.5 cm x width 39 cm x depth 6.5 cm
artworks.description: Enjoying a quiet, private moment, this young woman is absorbed in reading a letter in the morning light. She is still wearing her blue night jacket. All of the colours in the composition are secondary to its radiant lapis lazuli blue. Vermeer recorded the effects of light with extraordinary precision. Particularly innovative is his rendering of the woman’s skin with pale grey, and the shadows on the wall using light  blue.

artworks.title: A Windmill on a Polder Waterway, Known as ‘In the Month of July’
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 102 cm x width 66 cm x depth 14 cm
artworks.description: ‘Our country is saturated with colour. ... I repeat, our country is not grey, not even in grey weather, nor are the dunes grey’, wrote Constant Gabriël in a letter. Unlike many Hague School painters, he actually enjoyed depicting a beautiful summer day. There are even two of them in this painting: the image of the grass, sky and mill, and their reflection in the water.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers on a Marble Tabletop
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 48.5 cm x width 39.5 cm
artworks.description: This bouquet features more than ten species of flowers and teems with insects. As the blossoms flower at different times, it would be rather difficult to assemble such a bouquet in real life. Ruysch was well aware of this: her extensive study of live and prepared flowers allowed her to paint these vibrant bouquets with stunning precision. During her lifetime, she was one of the most celebrated painters of floral still lifes in Europe.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 81 cm x width 61 cm
artworks.description: In the 18th century, Van Huysum brought the extremely popular genre of flower painting to great heights. Instead of the usual dark background, he used a light one with a park landscape, creating the impression that the flowers are set out-of-doors on a balustrade. The décor here consists of a statue of Flora, the goddess of flowers, some cursorily painted foliage and a pond.

artworks.title: A Pelican and other Birds near a Pool, Known as ‘The Floating Feather’
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 159 cm x width 144 cm
artworks.description: It must have been a great honour for Hondecoeter to receive commissions from the country’s ruler. He made this regal bird scene for Het Loo, the palace of William and Mary. It features a pelican in the foreground, a cassowary behind it at the left, a flamingo and a black crowned crane. Water birds congregate in and around a basin, and a feather floats on the water’s surface.

artworks.title: Still Life with Asparagus
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, paper, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 25 cm x width 20.5 cm
artworks.description: Coorte produced mostly small, intimate still lifes. Through their simple subjects – asparagus or berries – these modest paintings stand out in stark contrast to the sumptuous still lifes that were in fashion at the time. While the aim of those works was to present a superabundance of costly objects and foodstuffs, here attention is focused on the refined rendering of a single vegetable.

artworks.title: Morning Ride along the Beach
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 43.7 cm x width 68.6 cm
artworks.description: Hague School painters were drawn to the harsh existence of poor fishermen, like those living in nearby Scheveningen. Here, however, Mauve depicted the other side of that fishing village: the sunny world of the well-to-do bourgeoisie. Three riders descend to the beach, where the bathing cabins stand ready for swimmers. The blond and blue colour scheme effectively conveys the briny atmosphere of a summer day along the seashore.

artworks.title: The Merry Family
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 110.5 cm x width 141 cm
artworks.description: The entire family is in high spirits, creating a ruckus: father, mother, and grandmother sing loudly, the children join in, and they even puff on long pipes. The note on the mantelpiece hints that there is a lesson to be learned from this painting: ‘As the old sing, so shall the young twitter.’ What is to become of the children if their parents set the wrong example?

artworks.title: Self-portrait
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 22.6 cm x width 18.7 cm × height 33.2 cm x width 29.3 cm x depth 5.9 cm
artworks.description: Even as an inexperienced young artist, Rembrandt did not shy away from experimenting. Here the light glances along his right cheek, while the rest of his face is veiled in shadow. It takes a while to realize that the artist is gazing intently out at us. Using the butt end of his brush, Rembrandt made scratches in the still wet paint to accentuate the curls of his tousled hair.

artworks.title: Isaac and Rebecca, Known as ‘The Jewish Bride’
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, linen (material), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 121.5 cm x width 166.5 cm
artworks.description: To prevent being killed and having his wife captured by King Abimelech, Isaac concealed his love for Rebecca by pretending they were brother and sister. However, their intimacy betrayed them when they thought they were not being spied on. Rembrandt depicts them in a tender moment. Furthermore, he works with exceptional freedom, applies the paint thickly, and scratches into it with the butt end of his paintbrush.

artworks.title: Still Life with Cheese
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 82.5 cm x width 111.4 cm
artworks.description: Fruit, bread, and cheese – grouped by type – are set on a table covered with costly damask tablecloths. The illusion of reality is astounding; the pewter plate extending over the edge of the table seems close enough to touch. The Haarlem painter Floris van Dijck ranked among the  pioneers of Dutch still-life painting.

artworks.title: Still Life with a Gilt Cup
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 87.8 cm x width 112.6 cm
artworks.description: The range of grey tonalities that Willem Heda could paint is astounding. With this subtle palette, he deftly rendered the objects – of pewter, silver, damask, glass and mother-of-pearl – on this table. A few yellow and ochre accents compliment this refined interplay of colours. Heda specialized in near monochromatic still lifes, so-called ‘tonal banquet pieces’.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 39 cm x width 31 cm × depth 7.5 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met bloemen. Op een plint staat een vaas met een boeket bloemen (anjers, viooltjes en dahlia's).

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers in a Glass
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, copper (metal), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 24.5 cm x width 19 cm
artworks.description: So many flowers in a small glass of water! This must have made an exceedingly lavish impression on a 17th-century viewer. Flowers were expensive at the time; gardens would have had only a few flowers, surrounded by much greenery. Jan Brueghel II was a faithful follower of his father Jan Brueghel I. This sparkling still life is a variant of a painting by his father.

artworks.title: The Love Letter
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: weight 9 kg × height 44 cm x width 38.5 cm × height 68.5 cm x width 62.5 cm x thickness 7 cm
artworks.description: Vermeer chose an unusual vantage point for this painting. From a dim space in the foreground, a glimpse is afforded of another room with a domestic scene. An elegantly dressed woman looks up expectantly at a maidservant, who has just handed her a letter. The seascape on the wall behind them may well allude to the epistle’s subject: during the 17th century, the sea was often compared to love, and the lover to a ship.

artworks.title: Portrait of a Girl Dressed in Blue
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 82 cm x width 66.7 cm
artworks.description: Why is this portrait so popular? Because it depicts an adorable child dressed in her Sunday best? As was the custom of the day, the young girl is portrayed as a small adult lady. That she is playing a role is betrayed only by her facial expression. Unfortunately, we know nothing about her identity or her family. Perhaps she resided in Haarlem, like the portraitist Verspronck.

artworks.title: Self-portrait as the Apostle Paul
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 91 cm x width 77 cm
artworks.description: Rembrandt is 55 years old in this self-portrait, and he still looks at himself candidly. Here he assumes the guise of a personage from the Bible, the Apostle Paul. The sword protruding from his cloak and the manuscript in his hands are the apostle’s customary attributes. By using his own face, Rembrandt encouraged the viewer to engage personally with the saint.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers in a Greek Vase: Allegory of Spring
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 149 cm x width 116 cm
artworks.description: Van Os spent his career mainly in Paris, where he painted porcelain for the famous Sèvres factory. At the same time, he created a furore with magnificently painted floral still lifes incorporating antique art objects. These two paintings probably belong to a series of the Four Seasons. In this painting of Spring, the flowers are arranged in a Greek vase.

artworks.title: Banquet Still Life
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 186 cm x width 243 cm
artworks.description:
The Fleming Adriaen van Utrecht here demonstrated that he could paint virtually anything, from costly tableware to glass, fruit, an enormous lobster on a Chinese plate, a cut-open pasty, and much more. Given
its striking low vantage point, this large painting was most likely meant to hang above a chimneypiece.

artworks.title: The Windmill at Wijk bij Duurstede
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 83 cm x width 101 cm
artworks.description: The windmill rises up majestically, defying the dark rain clouds and overshadowing the castle and the church of Wijk bij Duurstede. The River Lek flows in the foreground. This painting is world famous, and rightly so. In this impressive composition, Ruisdael united all the typical Dutch elements – the low-lying land, the water and the expansive sky – manipulating them to converge on the equally characteristic Dutch mill.

artworks.title: Square Man
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), linen (material)
artworks.dimensions: height 120.5 cm x width 118 cm x depth 4 cm
artworks.description: Cobra Group artists, like Karel Appel, were looking for a new way of painting after the Second World War and spontaneity was the key word. Appel tested the physical limits of the canvas while painting: this man just barely fits in the almost square surface. It is unclear whether he is impertinently horning in, or walking towards us, stripped of his clothes by some terrible event.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers
artworks.artist: Balthasar van der Ast (signed by artist)
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: frame: height 75.8 cm x width 59.8 cm × support: height 59 cm x width 43 cm
artworks.description:
A magnificent bouquet of tulips, roses, iris, columbine and gillyflowers is set in a ribbed glass vase. The artist
first made a detailed drawing on the prepared panel before beginning to paint. In the intervening centuries,
some of the pigments, primarily the lighter colours, have become transparent, allowing the underdrawing
to show through.

artworks.title: La Corniche near Monaco
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 75 cm x width 94 cm
artworks.description: In Monet’s time La Corniche was a narrow mountain track; nowadays, it is the main road between Nice and Monaco. Here the sun is high, the lone walker’s shadow short. Monet’s colours glisten: red, green, blue – everything shimmers in the sunlight. The painting was given to the Rijksmuseum already in 1900, when Monet’s work was still entirely unknown in the Netherlands.

artworks.title: Festoon of Fruit and Flowers
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 74 cm x width 60 cm
artworks.description: In 1626 this Utrecht-born painter moved to Antwerp, where he became acquainted with sumptuous and colourful Flemish still-life painting. He combined this influence with his gift for rendering nature in minute detail. This is clear to see in this floral and fruit festoon: a highly decorative entity that is nevertheless meticulously detailed. All kinds of hungry insects populate this still life.

artworks.title: View of the Golden Bend in the Herengracht
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), hardwood, biological material, oak (wood), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 42.5 cm x width 57.9 cm
artworks.description: Amsterdam’s huge population growth required it to expand in the 17th century: the city’s rings of canals were dug in phases. This is Herengracht under construction, with some plots still undeveloped. This particular section of the canal became the preserve of the very rich. They and their heirs were often mayors of the city and sat on the boards of the VOC, the WIC and the Suriname Society.

artworks.title: A Ship on the High Seas Caught by a Squall, Known as ‘The Gust’
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 77 cm x width 63.5 cm x height 90.5 cm x width 78.5 cm x depth 6.5 cm
artworks.description: This large, 70-gun British warship is in distress. A fierce gust of wind has broken one of its masts, and a sail has come loose. In 1672, Willem van de Velde II, together with his father, who was also a marine painter, entered the service of the English court. He made this painting and its companion, The Cannon Shot, in England.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 71.5 cm x width 52.5 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met bloemen op een stenen plint. Boeket met rozen, tulpen, narcissen, irissen, duizendschoon en koekoeksbloemen. Tussen de bloemen ook enkele vlinders, rechts een boek.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 6.5 cm × height 73 cm x width 60 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met bloemen. Bloemstuk met tulpen, anjers, rozen, papavers, kamperfoelie en irissen, op de achtergrond een landschap met een boog.

artworks.title: Flowers
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 5 cm × height 53.5 cm x width 76.5 cm
artworks.description: Een aardewerken pot met een boeket bloemen: tulpen, pioenrozen, violen en andere soorten. Ook links en rechts van het boeket verschillende takken met bloemen. Waarschijnlijk een dessus-de-porte.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers in a Glass Vase
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 65 cm x width 53.5 cm
artworks.description: Rachel Ruysch was the most famous female artist of her time. Monumental, opulent floral still lifes like this painting attracted the attention of wealthy patrons willing to pay prices exceeding 1000 guilders for them. The Elector of the Palatinate, a German principality, appointed her court painter. Even following her marriage, during which she bore ten children, Ruysch continued to work and signed her paintings with her own name.

artworks.title: The Singel Bridge at the Paleisstraat in Amsterdam
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: weight 39.4 kg × height 100 cm x width 152 cm
artworks.description: Breitner often took photographs to prepare his paintings, and several such studies are known for this work. The way in which the woman walks straight towards us and the image is cropped strikes one as distinctly photographic. Breitner initially depicted the woman as a maid, but after a negative review, the gallery representing him felt it would be better if he made her into an elegant lady.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers in a Wan-Li Vase
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, copper (metal), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 31 cm x width 22.5 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met bloemen in een Wan-Li-vaas. Boeket met tulpen, rozen en narcissen in een vaas. Op de stenen plint een anjer en een cyclaam.

artworks.title: The Sampling Officials of the Amsterdam Drapers’ Guild, Known as ‘The Syndics’
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 191.5 cm x width 279 cm
artworks.description: After suffering financial difficulties in the 1650s, Rembrandt moved to a rental house on the Rozengracht. The Amsterdam élite no longer knocked on his door as often as they had done before. He nevertheless remained popular: this important guild commissioned him to paint a group portrait. Rembrandt produced a lively scene by having the wardens look up from their work as if interrupted by our arrival.

artworks.title: The Sea
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 74.7 cm x width 65.9 cm
artworks.description: Jan Toorop made this seascape in Katwijk, where he was living in 1887. It is painted partly with a paintbrush and partly with a palette knife, as can be seen in the flat strokes. Through this technique, he succeeded in suggesting the effect of the waves breaking on the seashore in a realistic, almost tangible way. But if you look more closely, you can see a fantastic medley of colours.

artworks.title: Woman in a Large Hat
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: support: height 91.9 cm x width 81.7 cm
artworks.description: The plums in the basket and the woman’s subtly exposed shoulder imbue the painting with an erotic undertone. The type of hat atop her head was mostly worn by Romani women at the time. Such hats were worn at the court in The Hague during costume parties and parades. Van Everdingen enjoyed recognition at court, having received several commissions from it.

artworks.title: Portrait of a Woman, Probably Maria Trip (1619-1683)
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 107 cm x width 82 cm
artworks.description:
The sitter is likely the 20-year-old Maria Trip. She hailed from an extremely wealthy family involved in the arms trade. Here, she displays her affluence in full regalia: she wears a collar of the finest lace, a brooch with matching earrings, and a fortune in pearls.
The Chinese folding fan in her left hand was still a very rare and therefore precious accessory in 1639.

artworks.title: A Mother Delousing her Child’s Hair, Known as ‘A Mother’s Duty’
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 52.5 cm x width 61 cm
artworks.description: A mother thoroughly inspects her child’s head for lice. She pursues her task in a sober Dutch interior, with Delft blue tiles and a box bed. In the right foreground is a ‘kakstoel’, or potty chair. Through the doorway is a glimpse of a sunny back room and a garden. De Hooch specialized in such ‘through-views’.

artworks.title: Portrait of Alida Christina Assink
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 206 cm x width 149 cm
artworks.description:
This portrait of Alida Assink presents her in her finest attire, depicted from head to toe. That is quite exceptional, as the painter Kruseman typically reserved such a full-length portrait exclusively for royalty. Assink was 23 years old when this likeness was commissioned by her guardian, a wealthy landowner. The rural setting with hunting dog and garden vase harks back to the
English portrait style, which Kruseman admired.

artworks.title: Still Life with Roses
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 6.5 cm × height 39 cm x width 33 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met rozen. Hierbij ook een vlinder en twee slakken.

artworks.title: The Battle of Waterloo
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: length 565.7 cm × length 822.7 cm × length 825.7 cm x width 555.1 cm x depth 10 cm × length 900 cm x length 842 cm x width 40 cm × length 566.4 cm × height 567 cm x width 823 cm × length 822.6 cm × length 650 cm x length 592 cm x width 40 cm
artworks.description: Here the Duke of Wellington is receiving the message that Prussian forces are coming to his aid. Wellington, commander of the Anglo-Dutch troops, is the central figure in this group portrait of the major players at Waterloo. Lying wounded on a stretcher in the left foreground is the Dutch Crown Prince, later King William II. Originally intended for Wellington, the painting remained in the Netherlands thanks to William I who bought the picture for his son.

artworks.title: Still Life of Fruit and Flowers
artworks.artist: Balthasar van der Ast (signed by artist)
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 39.2 cm x width 69.8 cm
artworks.description: This still life invites close examination of all the details and elicits marvel at the richness of God’s creation: the colourful flowers, the exotic shells, but certainly also the beautiful insects. At the same time, decay is spreading. Fruit shows the first rotten spots, leaves are eaten away by caterpillars and snails and ants drag a dead fly. The painting is thus also about impermanence.

artworks.title: Portrait of William I, Prince of Orange
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 68 cm x width 55 cm x depth 5.5 cm × height 48 cm x width 35 cm
artworks.description: Of the noblemen who rebelled against Phillip II’s Spanish rule of the Netherlands, William of Orange rose to become the great leader of the Dutch Revolt. He defended his own interests, strove for greater independence and advocated freedom of religion. In 1580 Phillip II put a price on his head, and he was assassinated four years later.

artworks.title: The Menagerie
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 135 cm x width 116.5 cm
artworks.description: Presented here are two squirrel monkeys from Central America, two white sulphur-crested cockatoos from Australia, a grey parrot from Africa and a purple-naped lory – on a chain at the lower left – from Indonesia. Hondecoeter combined these creatures and several other splendid birds in this painting, which was destined for Het Loo, the palace of William III. It hung above the door of the king’s private apartment.

artworks.title: River Landscape with Riders
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 128.7 cm x width 227.8 cm × outer size: depth 10 cm (support incl. frame)
artworks.description: This is a panoramic, sun-drenched river landscape – somewhat hazy in the distance – with sketchily drawn clouds. Two Dutch officers halt at the river, and water their horses next to a herder and his resting cattle. This idyllic scene does not unfold in Italy, but along the Waal between Nijmegen and Cleves, where Cuyp made landscape drawings that he took back to his workshop in Dordrecht.

artworks.title: Ice-Skating in a Village
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: frame: height 54.3 cm x width 89 cm x depth 8.5 cm × support: height 35.7 cm x width 70.4 cm x thickness 1.4 cm
artworks.description: IJsvermaak bij een dorp. Dorpsgezicht in de winter met vele figuren die op het ijs schaatsen, spelen en kolven. Links zijn twee personen door het ijs gezakt. In de verte een ophaalbrug en een molen.

artworks.title: Sprig of White Currants with Insects
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, copper (metal), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: outer size: height 20.1 cm x width 23.6 cm x depth 2.5 cm (support incl. frame) × support: height 10.9 cm x width 14.6 cm
artworks.description: This scene is painted on a copper panel. Its smooth surface was well suited to meticulous and detailed finish. Van Kessel made dozens of such little ‘coppers’ of insects and other animals, which he would arrange in a larger composition. They may have also served as decorative panels for a small cabinet of curiosities.

artworks.title: Banquet at the Crossbowmen’s Guild in Celebration of the Treaty of Münster
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 232 cm x width 547 cm
artworks.description: 18 June 1648: a banquet is taking place at the Amsterdam crossbowmen’s guild. The occasion was the signing of the Treaty of Münster, which marked an end to the war with Spain. The captains of the civic guard company shake hands as a sign of peace, and the drinking horn is passed around. The poem on the drum proclaims the joy of Amsterdam’s armed militia that their weapons can henceforth be laid to rest.

artworks.title: Fishing for Souls
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 98.5 cm x width 187.8 cm × frame: height 121.1 cm x width 211 cm × sight size: height 97 cm x width 186.7 cm
artworks.description: In 1614 politics and religion are inextricably bound up with one another, as is very clear to see in this painting. At the left are Protestant ministers and leaders of the Republic (including Maurice), and at the right the archdukes who govern the South, with countless Catholic clergymen. The North, according to the painter, has a promising future: the sun shines there, the trees are full of leaves. Whosoever wants to be saved is better off swimming to a Protestant boat.

artworks.title: Portrait of a Married Couple, Likely Isaac Abrahamsz Massa and Beatrix van der Laen
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 140 cm x width 166.5 cm
artworks.description: It was rare for a married couple to be portrayed lifesize and together in a single painting, and even more so in such an intimate and joyful manner. The patron would have had to have been receptive to such innovation. The close friendship between Hals and the newlywed couple, presumably Isaac Abrahamsz Massa and Beatrix van der Laen, likely played a crucial role in facilitating the creation of this audacious portrait.

artworks.title: Mary Magdalene
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 86.5 cm x width 96 cm x thickness 5.5 cm × support: height 66.3 cm x width 76 cm
artworks.description: Mary Magdalene can be recognized by the jar of ointment in her hands with which she cared for Jesus’ feet following her conversion to Christianity. She is usually depicted as a prostitute, referencing her alleged past. The influence of Italian painting, which Van Scorel encountered during a sojourn in Rome and Venice, is evident in her clothing.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 67 cm x width 52.5 cm × depth 6 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met bloemen. Een boeket bloemen in een metalen vaas staande in een nis. In het boeket zitten rozen, irissen, papavers, een tarwehalm, tulpen en ander bloemen. Tussen de bloemen en over de nis kruipen een slak, een rups en een kever. Pendant van SK-A-337.

artworks.title: Donkey Rides on the Beach
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 51 cm x width 70 cm
artworks.description: In contrast to Hague School painters, Isaac Israels depicted the carefree, touristic aspect of the seaside resort of Scheveningen. He often used models for these scenes – in this case, his acquaintances Suze Pont, Agatha Pauw and her little sister. Israels worked rapidly: ‘Never work too much, no more than two hours at a stretch, do not fuss too long, otherwise you will lose your freshness.’

artworks.title: Young Italian Woman, with ‘Puck’ the Dog
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 144 cm x width 103 cm
artworks.description: Known as Fortunata, this woman was one of the many professional Italian models working in Paris in the late 19th century. Schwartze started this painting while sojourning there in 1884 and exhibited it a year later in Amsterdam, having added the dog in the meanwhile. For a young female artist at the time, studying in Paris was as unconventional as pursuing a career as an artist. However, Schwartze pressed on and became a highly successful portraitist.

artworks.title: Portrait of Marten Soolmans
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 207.5 cm x width 132 cm x depth 3.7 cm
artworks.description: Marten and Oopjen are the only couple that Rembrandt painted life-size, standing, and at full-length. Marten’s father came to Amsterdam from Antwerp as a Protestant refugee. He made his fortune as the owner of a sugar refinery. Marten married Oopjen in 1633. He was 20 and a law student, ready for a career in politics. Sadly, he died a mere eight years later.

artworks.title: Portrait of Oopjen Coppit
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 207.5 cm x width 132 cm x depth 3.6 cm
artworks.description: Oopjen was the eldest of three daughters of an old, affluent Amsterdam family. She sat to Rembrandt one year after her wedding with Marten. She was 23, and pregnant with her first child. The marriage represented an alliance between an established family and one of newcomers. This was celebrated with the commission of monumental likenesses from the city’s leading portraitist, namely Rembrandt van Rijn.

artworks.title: Woodland Pond at Sunset
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 22 cm x width 35 cm
artworks.description: Bilders painted this small panel in the vicinity of Lochem in the province of Gelderland. He was fasci-nated by the colours of nature and tried to recreate them as closely as possible. This painting is about the effect of the sunset, which is mirrored in the pond. The branches of the trees stand out starkly against the glowing sky.

artworks.title: Still Life with Golden Goblet
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 101.2 cm x width 84.7 cm × outersize: depth 9 cm (support incl. SK-L-5905)
artworks.description: Pieter de Ring (1615 - 1660). Still life with a golden cup.

artworks.title: Still Life with Lemon and Cut Glass
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 27 cm x width 23 cm × depth 8.2 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met een geschilde citroen in een kommetje, een geslepen glas en een bloementakje met een vlinder.

artworks.title: Still life with a Gilded Beer Tankard
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 45.5 cm x width 62.1 cm × outer size: depth 8.5 cm (support incl. frame)
artworks.description: Stilleven met een omgevallen zilveren drinkschaal, een roemer met wijn, een beker met deksel en tinnen borden met een geschilde citroen.

artworks.title: The Merry Fiddler
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 107.2 cm x width 88.3 cm
artworks.description: The man wearing extravagant Italian-looking clothing takes us by surprise. He appears from behind a tapestry and leans out of the window. He tries to engage with the viewer in order to clink glasses. So lifelike and convincing is Honthorst’s rendering that the fiddler seems to have slipped out from the frame of the painting to join us.

artworks.title: Winter Landscape
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 62 cm x width 75 cm
artworks.description: For this winter landscape, Koekkoek chose a hilly region in Gelderland or the German region of the Lower Rhine. Unlike his imposing forest views, this is a peaceful scene, with men pausing beside a sled laden with brushwood and vegetables. A panorama stretches out through the mist in the distance. The painting shows tranquil view of nature on a winter’s day, a world blanketed in a layer of pristine snow.

artworks.title: View of Olinda, Brazil
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 107.5 cm x width 172.5 cm
artworks.description: Frans Post mainly drew and painted landscapes and buildings, including the cathedral of Olinda, a coastal town in the Pernambuco region of Brazil. The building was badly damaged when the Dutch conquered this region. In the foreground, Post depicted an array of animals, including a monkey, a sloth, and an anteater. This animal motif continues in the 17th-century frame, which Post may have designed himself.

artworks.title: Italian Landscape with a Draughtsman
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 188.5 cm x width 240.4 cm
artworks.description: Our eye meanders happily through this large painting. If we follow the road and cross the bridge, we see in the distance a well-to-do traveller in a sedan chair. Mules carry his baggage. By placing a draughtsman near the bridge over the waterfall, Both would have us believe that he painted this scene from life, but in reality it was painted at home in his Dutch studio.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 65 cm x width 51.5 cm × depth 6 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met bloemen. Boeket met tulpen, irissen, rozen, stokrozen en anjers in een glazen vaas.

artworks.title: Flowers in a Terra Cotta Vase
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 8.5 cm × height 67 cm x width 52.5 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met bloemen in een terracotta vaas.

artworks.title: Still Life with a Turkey Pie
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 76.5 cm x width 135 cm
artworks.description: The Flemish painter Pieter Claesz fled to the Northern Netherlands in the beginning of the 17th century. He painted a table abounding with luxury products from all over the world: Zeeland oysters, Chinese porcelain, a nautilus shell from the Pacific Ocean, and pepper from India. Turkey originally came from North America. Along with other spices, nutmeg was used in the savoury turkey pie seen here. This popular spice  was cultivatedin the Moluccas (Southeast Asia), by enslaved people.

artworks.title: Portrait of Gerard Andriesz Bicker
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 117.5 cm x width 96 cm × height 94 cm x width 70.5 cm
artworks.description: Like his father, the twenty-year-old Gerard Bicker is portrayed as self-assured, his arm akimbo. The striking differences in the garments worn by father and son confirm that they are from different generations. While his father Andries is dressed in dignified black clothing with an old-fashioned ruff, Gerard wears a colourful and showy outfit with a flat collar and elegant gloves. Gerard was not awarded as many key administrative positions in Amsterdam.

artworks.title: Cartouche Decorated with Swags and Sprays of Flowers
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 99.3 cm x width 65 cm
artworks.description: Een stenen buste van Flora in een ornamentale cartouche omringd met een festoen van verschillende soorten bloemen, waaronder tulpen, rozen, ridderspoor, vingerhoedskruid, stokrozen, anjers en klimop.

artworks.title: Landscape with a Stone Bridge
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 29.5 cm x width 42.5 cm x depth 5.5 cm
artworks.description: Rembrandt painted only a few landscapes, mostly imaginary mountain scenes. Although The Stone Bridge is composed of elements studied from reality, it probably does not represent a specific place. The painting’s magical quality derives from its dramatic illumination: a beam of sunlight breaks through the clouds, making the approaching storm seem twice as menacing.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 113.7 cm x width 86.4 cm
artworks.description: Studio of Jan Brueghel I (1568 - 1625). Still life with flowers. Gift of Mr and Mrs Kessler -Hülsmann, 1940.

artworks.title: The Overturned Bouquet
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 89.5 cm x width 71.5 cm
artworks.description:
The ultimate challenge facing a 17th-century still-life painter was to render various materials in a convincing fashion. Everything had to appear real: a contemporary aptly coined this as ‘semblance without being’. Abraham Mignon was a master of such seeming realism. In this still life the cat playing with a mousetrap has upset a vase of flowers. Amongst the tulips, irises, poppies, and peonies can be discerned ants, spiders,
caterpillars, and snails.

artworks.title: The Fall of Man
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 273 cm x width 220 cm
artworks.description: In the left background we see God (a cloud with a human face and hands) cautioning Adam and Eve. They may eat the fruit of all of the trees, except the tree of ‘the knowledge of good and evil’. Tempted by the serpent (with a human torso), Adam and Eve nevertheless eat the  forbidden fruit, for which they were driven from Paradise.

artworks.title: Portrait of Marie Jeanette de Lange
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 70.5 cm x width 77.4 cm
artworks.description: Marie Jeanette de Lange chaired the Vereeniging voor Verbetering van Vrouwenkleding (Association for the Improvement of Women’s Clothing), which championed hygienic, loose-fitting, natural clothing that allowed women greater freedom of movement. In February 1900 she posed at home, dressed comfortably, for Jan Toorop. Using tiny dots of colourful paint, he created a sparkling portrait of a modern woman on the threshold of a new century.

artworks.title: The Feast of St Nicholas
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 82 cm x width 70.5 cm
artworks.description: The feast of St Nicholas takes place in December. In the Netherlands, it has been celebrated in the same way for centuries. Good children receive gifts from the saint. The little girl in the foreground, for instance, has a bucket full of treats. Naughty children, like the wailing boy at the left, get only a switch (a bundle of twigs) in their shoe. Jan Steen was a born storyteller. He succeeded in incorporating all of the elements of the popular feast in this picture.

artworks.title: Jeremiah Lamenting the Destruction of Jerusalem
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 58 cm x width 46 cm
artworks.description: The crestfallen Prophet Jeremiah rests his weary, old head on his hand. He laments Jerusalem going up in flames – in the background – whose destruction he had prophesied. Rembrandt heightened the sense of drama with powerful contrasts of light and dark. He derived the prophet’s bearded head from one of the old men he often etched around this time.

artworks.title: Cat at Play
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 12.3 cm × height 32.8 cm x width 45.2 cm x thickness 1.8 cm
artworks.description: A young cat plays with dominoes on a tabletop. At any moment an unexpected move could tip the ashtray with a burning cigar onto the ground – or worse. With this kind of endearing and amusing scenes Ronner became one of the most successful Dutch artists of her time. Her cat tableaux appealed to the sentimental love of her contemporaries for their pets.

artworks.title: Cows in the Meadow
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 13.5 cm × height 47 cm x width 70 cm
artworks.description: Landschap met koeien in de weide, op de voorgrond een paar eenden.

artworks.title: Forest Scene
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 136 cm x width 160 cm
artworks.description: Of all Dutch landscape painters, Koekkoek is perhaps the most Romantic. He specialized in splendid panora-mas of the valley of the Rhine and forest scenes with majestic trees, which at the time were called ‘Wodan’s Oaks’ (Wodan being the Dutch name for Odin, the major god in Norse mythology). In 1834 Koekkoek settled in Cleves in Germany, over the border from Nijmegen. He found German scenery, with its hills and the Rhine, more romantic than the Dutch landscape.

artworks.title: Still Life with Fruit, Oysters, and a Porcelain Bowl
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 55 cm x width 45 cm × depth 6.8 cm
artworks.description: The composition of this still life is both sumptuous and inventive. Mignon set the roemer, the green glass at the left, upside down. Reflected in it is a window, and a view of a church tower in Utrecht, where Mignon lived. The porcelain bowl from Asia was a sign of prosperity as well as being a showpiece on the table.

artworks.title: The Trekvliet Shipping Canal near Rijswijk, known as the ‘View near the Geest Bridge’
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 31 cm x width 50 cm
artworks.description: A tranquil landscape executed in bright colours: this early painting by Weissenbruch is still very Romantic in feel. Yet unlike the Romantic painters, Weissenbruch did not alter reality to suit his imagination, but gave a topographically accurate representation. The Trekvliet Canal linked The Hague with the neighbouring villages of Rijswijk and Voorburg. In the distance at left is the tower of De Binckhorst Castle, and the windmill called the Laakmolen at right.

artworks.title: Flowers from Normandy
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 72 cm x width 60 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met bloemen. Boeket bloemen in een hoge glazen vaas, rechts ligt een roos.

artworks.title: De welvoorziene keuken
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: weight 54.5 kg × height 171 cm x width 250 cm
artworks.description: The central theme of this painting is not the profuse display of vegetables, fruit, meat, poultry and pots and pans on offer by these kitchen maids. Instead it is Christ’s visit to Mary and Martha, which is depicted inconspicuously in the background. The contrast between the foreground and the background conceals the message of the painting: do not give in to earthly temptations.

artworks.title: Still Life with a Salt
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 52.6 cm x width 44.1 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met een brood en een vis op tinnen borden. Rechts een roemer, achteraan een zoutvat. Op tafel liggen ook een mes en enkele hazelnoten.

artworks.title: Decorative Depiction with Plants and Animals
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 226.6 cm x width 55.6 cm x depth 9.8 cm × height 218 cm x width 47 cm x thickness 3.5 cm x weight 8 kg
artworks.description: French school, c. 1775. Four decorative paintings with plants and animals.

artworks.title: Kalme zee
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 123.4 cm x width 97.5 cm x thickness 3.2 cm × depth 8 cm
artworks.description: Kalme zee. Vissersboten in ondiep water nabij de kust. Op de voorgrond waadt een man met een anker door het water.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 86 cm x width 68 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met bloemen. Boeket van bloemen (rozen, tulpen, irissen) in een glazen vaas op een stenen plint, met vlinders tussen de bloemen.

artworks.title: The Battle of Terheide
artworks.medium: textile materials, materials by function, canvas, ink
artworks.dimensions: height 170 cm x width 289 cm
artworks.description: To commemorate the Dutch naval commander Maerten Harpertsz Tromp, his family commissioned a series of pen paintings of Tromp’s best-known battles from Willem van de Velde. The artist used pen and ink on canvas for these works, which resemble meticulous, accurate engravings. Van de Velde witnessed the Battle of Terheide in 1653. He used the sketches that he produced on board as studies for this pen painting.

artworks.title: Madonna of Humility
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, tempera
artworks.dimensions: height 74 cm x width 52 cm
artworks.description: As a Dominican monk, Fra Angelico was not subject to the strict rules of the Florentine painters’ guild. He was thus free to develop a more personal style. This combined strong realism and solid forms with a certain sweetness partly derived from earlier Sienese and Florentine examples.

artworks.title: Missing Title
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 88.5 cm x width 110.5 cm × sight size: height 86.5 cm x width 108.7 cm
artworks.description: The two gnarled oak trees, brightly illuminated by a few rays of sunlight, stand out sharply against the threatening sky. Van Goyen drew the trees with his brush. He used thin, almost transparent paint for the foliage and thick, grainy paint for the furrowed trunks. The landscape’s near monochrome palette is enlivened by the blue and red doublets of the two figures resting.

artworks.title: On the Heath near Laren
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 118 cm x width 145.5 cm x depth 14.5 cm × height 77 cm x width 104 cm
artworks.description: From 1882 Mauve painted in Laren, a village located in barren heathlands, with only the occasional tree and shrub. Flocks of sheep on the heath were a popular subject. In his atelier Mauve incorporated the studies he had made en plein air into large compositions. These were popular on the English and American markets. His name became synonymous with ‘sheep paintings’.

artworks.title: VOC Senior Merchant with his Wife and an Enslaved Servant
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 137.3 cm x width 206.5 cm x thickness 4.2 cm (support incl. protective backboard) × outer size: depth 5 cm (support incl. frame)
artworks.description: The figure standing on the left is a Dutch East India Company (VOC) merchant, probably Jakob Martensen, beside his wife. Behind them is an enslaved man holding a parasol, a pajong, over their heads. This was a status symbol in Javanese culture. Batavia Castle is visible in the background. To the right, the Company fleet rides at anchor, ready to return to the Netherlands. The merchant points to the ships with his stick, indicating his involvement.

artworks.title: Decorative Depiction with Plants and Animals
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 218 cm x width 46 cm x thickness 3.5 cm x weight 8 kg × height 226.6 cm x width 55.6 cm x depth 9.8 cm
artworks.description: French school, c. 1775. Four decorative paintings with plants and animals.

artworks.title: The Tree of Jesse
artworks.artist: circle of Geertgen tot Sint Jans
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 89.8 cm x width 60.6 cm
artworks.description: Pictured here symbolically is Christ’s family tree. It grows out of the sleeping figure of Jesse, forefather of a line of kings that included, according to tradition, Salomon, David and Jesus.The branches are filled with the kings of Israel, among them King David with his harp. At top, the Virgin is enthroned with the Christ Child on her lap.

artworks.title: The Old Town Hall of Amsterdam
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 65.5 cm x width 84.5 cm
artworks.description:
Saenredam based this painting on a drawing he had made sixteen years earlier. On the step of the portico, he noted that the dilapidated town hall had in the meantime been destroyed by fire and replaced by a new monumental one (now the Palace on Dam Square). From 1658 this painting hung in the stately chamber
of the mayors in the new Town Hall as a memento of the old building.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers and Nuts
artworks.medium: paper, paint (coating), pasteboard, cardboard, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 50 cm × height 37.2 cm × width 44 cm x width 31.5 cm
artworks.description: Floral still lifes of the Romantic period are characterised by their simple composition, light colour and the profusion of native species. So too in this still life: we see authentic Dutch plants such as primulas, geraniums, periwinkles, forget-me-nots and nasturtiums, as well as plants that were cultivated in glasshouses around 1830: daffodils, anemones, tulips and hyacinths. The blue tulip was originally purple: remains of the lost red pigment are still visible.

artworks.title: Oostzijdse Mill along the River Gein by Moonlight
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 63 cm x width 75.4 cm
artworks.description: This landscape clearly reveals how indebted Mondrian was to the Hague School as a young artist. A few years earlier, he had copied Paul Gabriël’s In the Month of July in the Rijksmuseum (on view in this gallery). Although the compositions resemble each other, the general impression in each case is entirely different. Mondrian modified the lines and colours in order to create a non-realistic, decorative painting.

artworks.title: Still Life with Fruit
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 66.5 cm x width 52.5 cm x thickness 4 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met vruchten. In een stenen nis liggen druiven, perziken, pruimen en een meloen. Tussen het fruit enkele vlinders en rechts een koperen beeldje van een putto die een schaal draagt. Aan de bovenkant van de nis hangen een druiventros en kersen. Pendant van SK-A-336.

artworks.title: Battle of Gibraltar in 1607
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 136.8 cm x width 187 cm
artworks.description: A Spanish flagship is hit amidships by a smaller Dutch warship. It explodes in the middle of the Bay of Gibraltar. 25 April 1607: this is the first sea battle the Dutch fleet fights out with the Spanish beyond their own waters. It meets with great success. The Spanish losses are extensive: Spanish soldiers are catapulted into the air and drown in the sea. The painting is thus also meant to celebrate this spectacular Dutch victory.

artworks.title: 'The Little Seamstress'
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 13 cm × height 75.7 cm x width 61.2 cm x thickness 3.2 cm
artworks.description: 'Het naaistertje'. Een meisje zit een kledingstuk te verstellen. Links valt het licht door een venster naar binnen, het meisje heeft de voeten op een stoof. Rechts tegels op de muur.

artworks.title: Seascape near Heijst
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 4.8 cm × height 27.5 cm x width 55 cm x thickness 1.9 cm
artworks.description: Zeegezicht bij Heijst. Golven van de branding bij het strand, boven het water meeuwen.

artworks.title: Winter
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 14.6 cm x width 37.1 cm × outer size: height 22.8 cm x width 45.3 cm x depth 3.3 cm (support incl. frame)
artworks.description: Winter. Op het ijs rechts enkele schaatsers, in de verte gebouwen en molens. Links pissen en poepen enkele figuren tegen bomen, op de voorgrond een poepende hond. Onderdeel van een reeks met de vier jaargetijden, SK-A-1771/1774.

artworks.title: Winter Landscape
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 61.3 cm x width 69.1 cm x thickness 9 cm × height 42 cm x width 49.7 cm
artworks.description: Ruisdael painted around 25 winter landscapes. This scene is dominated by ominous dark clouds, and lit from the left by low, raking sunlight. The warmly dressed figures on the ice seem insignificant in the face of this inclement weather. A cheerful crowd of ice skaters would have been out of place in such a wintery landscape by Ruisdael.

artworks.title: The Castle of Batavia
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 108 cm x width 151.4 cm
artworks.description: These people would never have all been together at the same time! Beeckman was trying to give an overview of the different ethnic groups in Batavia. They include Japanese, Indians, ‘mardijkers’ – formerly enslaved people, recognizable by their striped clothing – and a Dutch-Eurasian couple and their enslaved servant with a pajong (sunshade). A Javanese woman sells fruit, a Chinese person is fishing and Moluccans play football with a rattan ball. This painting hung in the assembly room of the Dutch East India Company (VOC) headquarters in Amsterdam.

artworks.title: Autumn Landscape
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: width 66.5 cm × height 41.3 cm
artworks.description: Weissenbruch spent a great deal of time in the village of Noorden along the Nieuwkoop lakes, where he ventured out to sketch, even in poor weather. He worked up these sketches later in his studio. In Autumn Landscape the paint layers were applied wet-on-wet in an ultimate attempt to capture on canvas the damp atmosphere of the Dutch polder landscape.

artworks.title: Landscape with Waterfall
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 142.5 cm x width 196 cm
artworks.description: The tiny figures in this grand landscape with a rushing waterfall are almost lost. The composition is dominated by gnarled trees, barren tree trunks, and roiling water. The dramatic cycle of nature’s birth and decay is almost tangible. A church tower rises up in the distance like a beacon of peace.

artworks.title: Beach at Ebb Tide
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 35 cm x width 55 cm × height 60 cm x width 80.5 cm x depth 10.5 cm
artworks.description: Daubigny painted this beautiful seascape in Villerville-sur-Mer in Normandy. On an otherwise empty beach, a lone shell seeker walks along, with a basket on her back. Hague School painters greatly admired Daubigny. His broad brushstrokes and subtle colour nuances were ideally suited to depicting the Dutch landscape.

artworks.title: Shells and Marine Plants
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 9.3 cm × height 106.5 cm x width 86 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met exotische schelpen en enkele stukken koraal, bij elkaar liggend op een rots aan de kust.

artworks.title: Vase with Pink Flowers
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 46 cm x width 38 cm x thickness 1.2 cm × height 52 cm x width 43.5 cm x depth 7 cm
artworks.description: Schets van een vaas met rose bloemen over resten van een potloodtekening van huizen.

artworks.title: Still Life with Peacocks
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 145 cm x width 135.5 cm × height 170 cm x width 162.5 cm x thickness 5 cm
artworks.description: In Rembrandt’s time, peacocks were eaten by the well-to-do: the meat was incorporated into meat pies, among other dishes. Immediately after being killed, the birds were hung to bleed out, as Rembrandt shows us in this storeroom. He was doubtless captivated by the plumage’s splendid marks, the riot of colours: blue, green and yellow ochre.

artworks.title: Shepherdess with a Flock of Sheep
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 55.6 cm x width 82.7 cm x thickness 3 cm × depth 13.4 cm × weight 22 kg
artworks.description: Herderin met een kudde schapen in een boomgaard. De herderin staat rechts met een staf in de handen, bij haar staat een hond.

artworks.title: Baker’s Couple Arent Oostwaard and Catharina Keizerswaard
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 37.7 cm x width 31.5 cm
artworks.description: This baker’s couple from Leiden proudly proffer their freshly baked loaves and rolls. An old inscription on the back of the painting gives their names. The boy is also mentioned: he is the painter’s son. He may blow the horn to let people know the bread is ready. Jan Steen combined several genres in a single painting – it serves as a family portrait, a still life of bread, and a portrayal of a profession all at once.

artworks.title: The Canal at ’s-Graveland
artworks.artist: Pieter Gerardus van Os (mentioned on object)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 111.5 cm x width 89.5 cm
artworks.description: In 1817 the Amsterdam merchant Herman Waller com-missioned Van Os to paint two prospects of the village of ’s-Graveland, where Waller had a country house. Van Os painted this scene either from a window in Waller’s house or from the local inn. This high vantage point afforded an unusual perspective. The diagonal view of the ’s-Graveland canal also includes the garden, with a gardener and two dogs.

artworks.title: Interior with Women beside a Linen Cupboard
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 70 cm x width 75.5 cm
artworks.description: The sun lights up the canal houses outside, while in the darker interior a girl plays ‘kolf,’ a kind of hockey. Two women stack freshly pressed linen in a closet. The linen cupboard had an important place in the home. The lady of the house carried its key with her and ‘handed out the sheets’: she called the shots and was in charge of the household.

artworks.title: Seven Chicks
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: depth 3.5 cm × height 32 cm x width 38 cm
artworks.description: This oil sketch of chicks affords unique insight into the working method of Melchior d'Hondecoeter, the best-known bird painter of the 17th century. He used such studies as the basis for his monumental park landscapes, which feature diverse species of birds. Depicted in this sketch are seven chicks in various poses. They were frequently reused in a ‘copy & paste’ fashion in his paintings.

artworks.title: Militia Company of District VIII in Amsterdam under the Command of Captain Roelof Bicker
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 235 cm x width 750 cm
artworks.description: Civilians also served as armed guardsmen to defend their cities. The wealthiest among them were eager to have their portraits included in large civic guard paintings. This painting originally hung in the same hall of the Kloveniersdoelen (Arquebusiers’ Headquarters) as Rembrandt’s night Watch. We know everyone’s name except for the boy carrying a red cloak in the middle. He is the servant of the man beside him, holding a staff.

artworks.title: ‘Arrangement in Yellow and Gray’: Effie Deans
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 224.5 cm x width 124 cm × height 194 cm x width 93 cm x depth 9 cm
artworks.description: Whistler here connected painting with music and literature, alluded to by the title of this piece. He used the musical term ‘arrangement’ to draw attention to the composition of colours. Later on, he added the literary subtitle ‘Effie Deans’ after the heroine of a novel by the Scottish writer Walter Scott. The model posing for Whistler in this painting is Maud Franklin, who worked with him for more than fifteen years.

artworks.title: Lot and his Daughters
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 140 cm x width 204 cm
artworks.description: God decided to destroy the sinful city of Sodom, sparing only the righteous Lot and his family. Because Lot’s daughters were afraid of remaining childless – all of the men had perished – they got their father drunk and seduced him. Goltzius creates a striking contrast between the sunburned skin of the elderly Lot and the smooth skin of his two daughters.

artworks.title: Portrait of William I, King of the Netherlands
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 227 cm x width 155.5 cm
artworks.description: After the Battle of Waterloo, William Frederick, prince of Orange-Nassau and son of Stadholder William V, was inaugurated as King William I in 1815. Here he wears the full-dress uniform of a general, with the royal ermine cloak over it. He points to a map of Java in what was then the Dutch East Indies, where the portrait came to hang in the governor’s palace in 1821.

artworks.title: A Flemish Kermis with a Performance of the Farce ‘Een cluyte van Plaeyerwater’
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 112 cm x width 157 cm
artworks.description: Peeter Baltens, a painter in the circle of Pieter Bruegel, played an important role in the Antwerp artists’ guild. He was also a rederijker (rhetorician): a poet and an actor. A comic dramatic work is being performed on the makeshift stage in the middle of this kermis scene. The farce is about a man – hidden in a pedlar’s basket – who catches his wife cheating on him with a clergyman.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers and Fruit
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 40.3 cm x width 31.8 cm x thickness 1.7 cm × depth 7 cm
artworks.description: Jan Evert Morel (1777 - 1808). Still life with flowers and fruit.

artworks.title: Bluff-Bowed Scheveningen Boats at Anchor
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 11.5 cm × height 115.5 cm x width 80 cm
artworks.description: Scheveningse bommen voor anker. In het ondiepe water bij het strand liggen vier vissersschepen, bij de schepen staat een groep vissersvrouwen.

artworks.title: Still Life with Books in a Niche
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), textile materials, biological material, panel, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 30 cm x width 56 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met verschillende open en gesloten boeken liggend op een plank in een nis. In het midden een pennenkoker, rechts een ronde en een rechthoekige doos. Bovendeel van de linker zijpaneel met de profeet Jesaja, in het Museum Boijmans-Van Beuningen te Rotterdam. Het rechter zijpaneel bevindt zich in het Koninklijk Museum voor de Schone Kunsten te Brussel, het middenpaneel met de verkondiging is in de kerk Ste. Madelaine in Aix-en-Provence.

artworks.title: Rough Sea with Ships
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 4 cm × height 31.5 cm x width 39 cm
artworks.description: Woelige zee met schepen. Op de voorgrond een vissersbootje, rechts een tjalk, daarachter een oorlogsschip. Pendant van SK-A-2316.

artworks.title: The ‘Golden Bend’ in the Herengracht, Amsterdam, Seen from the West
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 59.7 cm x width 81 cm x depth 7 cm × height 40.5 cm x width 63 cm
artworks.description:
The cityscape developed into an independent genre only after 1650, with Berckheyde as one of its leading exponents. In this painting he recorded with mathematical precision the newly built houses along the ‘Golden Bend’, the most expensive stretch of Amsterdam’s
Herengracht. Through the omission of the row of young trees that lined the quay of the canal in reality, the topographical accuracy of the scene is complemented by a bit of artistic license.

artworks.title: Portrait of Elisabeth Bellinghausen (c.1520- after 1570)
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 34.5 cm x width 24.3 cm
artworks.description: Portret van Elisabeth Bellinghausen. Portret van de jonge vrouw, ten halven lijve, zittend achter een balustrade, in de rechterhand een takje bitterzoet. Om de hals een gouden ketting, om de middel een brede ceintuur met een gouden gesp. Zij draagt een met parels bestikt mutsje op het hoofd. De geportretteerde is een dochter van prof. Peter Bellinghausen, kanselier van Keulen. Het schilderij is een pendant van het portret van Jacobus Omphalius (1500-1567) in het Mauritshuis, Den Haag (inv.nr. 1225).

artworks.title: Portrait of a Member of the Van der Mersch Family
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 72 cm x width 57 cm
artworks.description: This portrait invites us to enter the room and enjoy art and music with this gentleman. Typical of the 18th century is the lack of distance between sitter and viewer: the likeness is not intimidating. We stand face to face with a cheerful young man, member of a wealthy Mennonite family from Amsterdam. The visit has caught him unawares: on his shoulder are traces of powder spilled while he powdered his wig.

artworks.title: Interior of the Church of St Bavo in Haarlem
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: outer size: depth 7 cm (support incl. frame) × support: height 93.7 cm x width 55.2 cm
artworks.description:
Saenredam specialized in architectural painting. He studied buildings closely, making detailed drawings of them, which he then reworked into paintings. Here he chose a vantage point from behind an arch, which creates a second framing element. Our gaze is automatically drawn upwards to the old organ, which has a painted scene of the Resurrection of Christ. This is a remnant of the by-then long-abolished Catholic
decoration.

artworks.title: Anemones
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 90 cm x width 46 cm × depth 12 cm
artworks.description: Verster brought the flower still-life genre to a new, modern height. The emphasis no longer lay on creating lavish displays of exotic blossoms, but rather on portraying light and the natural process of growth and decay. This still life is reminiscent of an autumn bouquet. The wilted yellowed leaves, the translucent petals and the black glass vase afforded the painter every opportunity to experiment with the light.

artworks.title: The Grey Horse
