artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), hardwood, biological material, oak (wood), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 43.9 cm x width 37.6 cm
artworks.description:
A grey horse, whose reins are held by a boy, plays the leading role in this small panel. The horse stands out
clearly against the dramatic cloudy sky. Wouwerman’s rendering of the animal with its almost palpable coat
is very lifelike. By choosing a low vantage point, the artist strengthened the painting’s monumental effect.

artworks.title: A January Evening in the Woods of The Hague
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 92 cm x width 121 cm × depth 16.5 cm
artworks.description: Gezicht in het Haagse Bos tijdens de winter. In het midden een houten bruggetje over een slootje.

artworks.title: Man Handing a Letter to a Woman in the Entrance Hall of a House
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 68 cm x width 59 cm
artworks.description:
All the windows and doors of this canal house are open. Daylight falls on the lady of the house, who is receiving a letter. With lighting effects and figures, De Hooch leads our gaze outside. We follow the dog to the canal and to a child playing with a whip, and
beyond towards the sunny street on the opposite side. The view continues through the gate on the right.

artworks.title: Michiel de Ruyter as Lieutenant-Admiral
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 157 cm x width 138 cm
artworks.description: In 1667 Ferdinand Bol painted several life-size portraits of Michiel de Ruyter. These were hung in the headquarters of all five Dutch admiralties. This painting went to Middelburg. De Ruyter’s hero status made him a powerful man. In the portrait he is richly dressed and holding his commander’s baton. Around his neck he is wearing the Order of St Michael, awarded to him by the King of France.

artworks.title: A Lion from the Menagerie of King Louis Napoleon, 1808
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 187 cm x width 138 cm × weight 56 kg
artworks.description: Een leeuw uit de menagerie van koning Lodewijk Napoleon. Staande leeuw, met geopende muil.

artworks.title: Adriaan van der Hoop’s Trotter ‘De Vlugge’ (The Fast One) in a Meadow
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 60 cm x width 54 cm
artworks.description: Upper-class Dutchmen aspired to the life of an English gentleman. The fabulously rich banker and art collector Adriaan van der Hoop owned racehorses and, like members of the English aristocracy, had portraits made of his prizewinners. The picture’s style is also English: the horse is painted in profile, in cool bright tones, set in a sober composition. The horse stands in a meadow in Van der Hoop’s estate near Haarlem.

artworks.title: Mary Magdalene
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, paper, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 31 cm x width 35 cm x thickness 1.3 cm × depth 8.5 cm
artworks.description: Kop van een jonge vrouw. Vormt samen met SK-A-4173 een borstbeeld van Maria Magdalena.

artworks.title: Still Life with Books
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 26.5 cm x width 41.5 cm × depth 5.5 cm
artworks.description:
Grey and brown tints dominate this composition, and a shadow spreads slowly over the wall. The painting
alludes to the fleetingness of life. The battered books allude to transience. The music produced by the lute
is momentary, a symbol of the brevity of life. A literal reference to death is inscribed on the sheet of paper
draped over the table’s edge: ‘finis’ ([the] end).

artworks.title: Young Woman, Gazing at the Sea
artworks.medium: paper, paint (coating), pasteboard, cardboard, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 2.3 cm × height 61.2 cm x width 45 cm
artworks.description: Isaac Israels was a frequent visitor to Paris, as is reflected in this summery portrait. He was one of the few Dutch artists to adopt the bright palette of the French Impressionists. And just like them he favoured subjects from modern life, such as this beach scene. Squinting in the light, this woman enjoys a moment in the sun, the blue of the sea echoed in her hat and white blouse.

artworks.title: Cornelis de Bruyn (1652-1727), Draftsman and Traveller
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 70.5 cm x width 59 cm
artworks.description: Sir Godfried Kneller (1646 - 1723). Cornelis de Bruyn (1652 - 1727). Artist and traveller.

artworks.title: Missing Title
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 13 cm × height 97 cm x width 127 cm
artworks.description: Gezicht op het Rokin en de Langebrug te Amsterdam.

artworks.title: The Saint Elizabeth’s Day Flood
artworks.artist: Master of the St Elizabeth Panels
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 127.3 cm x width 109.5 cm x height 125.4 cm x width 108.6 cm
artworks.description: On the night of 19 November 1421 – the feast day of Saint Elizabeth – much of Holland was flooded. The Dordrecht region was badly hit: 23 villages were submerged and 2,000 people died. The survivors later had an altarpiece made. The outer panels depict the disaster, with the breach of the dike on the right and the undamaged town of Dordrecht on the left.

artworks.title: View of the Oosterpark, Amsterdam, in the Snow
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 70 cm × width 122 cm
artworks.description: The winter of 1892 was exceptionally severe. From the studio of his friend Witsen, Breitner could see the snow-covered Oosterpark (then under construction), located in a new district of Amsterdam. Typical tall, late 19th-century houses are visible on the horizon. Breitner, always short of money, is said to have traded this painting for a bicycle rather than sell it through the dealer to whom he was under contract.

artworks.title: Javanese Court Officials
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), textile materials, inorganic material, cotton (textile), paper, oil paint (paint), gilding (material)
artworks.dimensions: depth 4.5 cm × height 196.8 cm x width 74.3 cm
artworks.description: These five figures are representatives of the Javanese elite. The accurately depicted clothing and batik motifs signal where they come from and what their rank and status are. Knowledge of their etiquette and appearance was of great political importance to the colonial administration. The Javanese elite was increasingly deployed to control and exploit the colony in the first half of the 19th century.

artworks.title: Landscape with a Thunderstorm Brewing
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 90.2 cm x width 139.8 cm × depth 12 cm
artworks.description: This landscape is full of drama and contrasts. Such impressive views were very popular in the first half of the 19th century. Whether they presented a realistic scene was irrelevant; they were made to convey the grandeur and power of nature and to strike an emotional chord.

artworks.title: 'Felsenmeer'
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 43.6 cm x width 55.1 cm x depth 9.8 cm × height 35 cm x width 46.5 cm
artworks.description: Voorstelling getiteld 'Felsenmeer'. Bosgezicht met dunnen stammen tussen rotsen.

artworks.title: 'The Anemic Lady'
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 69.5 cm x width 55 cm × depth 7 cm
artworks.description: 'De bleekzuchtige dame'. Interieur met een zieke jonge vrouw zittend op een stoel naast een tafel voor een bedstee. Onder haar voet heeft ze een stoof, rechts zit een kat. Achter de vrouw houdt een dokter een kolk met urine tegen het licht, naast hem staat een man. Links leidt een trap naar andere kamers, boven de deur hangt een schilderij. In de achterste kamer een haard met een mantelstuk.

artworks.title: Gallant Conversation, Known as ‘The Paternal Admonition’
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 85 cm x width 87 cm x thickness 8.5 cm × height 71 cm x width 73 cm
artworks.description:
The standing woman is receiving two guests. The man seems to have just arrived, as he still holds his hat in his hand. Ter Borch excelled in accurately rendering fabrics, such as the satin dress. Furthermore, he favoured ambiguous scenes, whereby the sentiments
of his figures are difficult to determine. Here, too, the reason behind the gathering remains enigmatic.

artworks.title: Forest Landscape in the Moonlight
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 10 cm × height 70.5 cm x width 110.5 cm x thickness 3 cm
artworks.description: Boslandschap bij maanlicht. Twee herten staan bij de oever van een meertje.

artworks.title: Meadow near Oosterbeek
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 39 cm x width 55 cm × height 66.7 cm x width 81.7 cm x thickness 11 cm
artworks.description: During the summers in the 1860s, a group of painters gathered to work directly from nature in Oosterbeek, in the province of Gelderland. There, the Veluwe ridge of hills meets the low, broad valley of the Rhine. The generation of artists active before Bilders, the painters of the Romantic period, delighted in capturing that contrast. Bilders, however, singled out the ‘ordinary’ meadows in the forelands of the Rhine.

artworks.title: Salome with the Head of John the Baptist
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: depth 16 cm × height 120 cm x width 90 cm
artworks.description: Salome is a biblical ‘femme fatale’ par excellence: she was responsible for the death of John the Baptist. Because Salome danced so beautifully for King Herod, he granted her a wish. In consultation with her mother, Herodias, Salome asked for John’s head on a platter. They thus ensured John’s demise for having criticized Herodias’ marriage.

artworks.title: Saul and the Witch of Endor
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: painted surface: height 87 cm x width 121.6 cm × frame: height 104.2 cm x width 138.9 cm x thickness 5 cm × support: height 85.5 cm x width 122.8 cm
artworks.description: Fearing the outcome of a battle, Saul, king of the Israelites, consulted the fortune-telling witch of Endor. The prophecy came true: Saul lost the battle, but shortly before he was to be killed, he threw himself on his sword. His suicide – in the middle background – is a warning against witchcraft. In the foreground is a Witches’ Sabbath: the fortune-teller sits within a chalk circle, surrounded by other witches, satyrs, and imaginary figures.

artworks.title: Ophélie, la cape bleue sur les eaux (Ophelia with a Blue Wimple in the Water)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), chalk, inorganic material, paper, oil paint (paint), pastel (crayon)
artworks.dimensions: height 54.5 cm x width 49.5 cm × depth 2.5 cm
artworks.description: Around 1900 young artists exhibited at various independent societies. Les Vingt in Brussels was such an association, of which both James Ensor and Jan Toorop were members and where Redon was invited to show his work. His dreamy, visionary art is part of Symbolism. Here he depicted the fatal drowning of Ophelia, the lover of Hamlet from the Shakespearean tragedy of the same title.

artworks.title: Bathsheba at her Toilet
artworks.artist: Cornelis Cornelisz. van Haarlem (mentioned on object)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 99.5 cm x width 85 cm x thickness 5 cm × height 77.5 cm x width 64 cm
artworks.description: Bathsheba bathes out of doors assisted by two maidservants. King David spies the young woman from the roof of his palace and instantly falls in love. In this painting, the king remains unseen as Cornelisz van Haarlem depicted the Old Testament story from his point of view. We, the viewers, assume the role of David spying on the three nude women.

artworks.title: Gezicht vanaf de Rapenburgwal op de Peperbrug en het pakhuis Sweeden
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 52 cm x width 42 cm
artworks.description: Stadsgezicht met pakhuis, Rapenburg 2. Rechts een ijzeren ophaalbrug over de Rapenburgwal, een platte schuit ligt aangemeerd bij het pakhuis.

artworks.title: The Raampoortje in Amsterdam
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 57 cm x width 48 cm
artworks.description: The 18th-century Raampoortje was part of Amsterdam’s city rampart near the Bloemgracht. The small gate gave access to the bleaching fields outside the city wall, where dyed cloth was laid out to dry on wooden frames, from which the Raampoortje (Frame Gate) got its name. Here we look from the bleaching fields past the houses on the Bloemgracht towards the cold and wintry city. The Westertoren rises in the distance. The gate was demolished in 1846.

artworks.title: The Zuiderhavendijk, Enkhuizen
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 9 cm × height 50 cm x width 65 cm
artworks.description: De Zuiderhavendijk in Enkhuizen met zicht op het Zuiderspui. In de gracht een man in een boot, op straat een voerman die zijn paard voert, rechts een groentewinkel.

artworks.title: Cows at a Pond
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 27.5 cm x width 45.3 cm × depth 7.2 cm × weight 6 kg
artworks.description: Landschap met koeien bij een plas.

artworks.title: Vanitas still life
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 57 cm x width 70 cm × depth 6 cm
artworks.description: Vanitas stilleven. Op een tafel liggen een viool, een schedel, een liedboek, een inktstel, een verfrommeld brief met zegel, boeken, een zandloper en een tas met documenten. Aan de muur een smeulende olielamp.

artworks.title: Ships before the Coast
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 42 cm x width 46 cm × depth 4.5 cm
artworks.description: In the 17th century painters specialized in specific genres. For instance, Willem van de Velde became a marine painter, perhaps even the most successful one ever. He portrayed large, spectacular naval battles as well as small, tranquil coastal views, like we see here. Modest commercial vessels lie still on the smooth-as-glass surface of the water. Somewhat further back in the middle ground are two warships calmly awaiting what is to come.

artworks.title: Portraits of Giuliano and Francesco Giamberti da Sangallo
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 47.5 cm x width 33.5 cm
artworks.description: This exceptional diptych shows the leading Florentine architect Giuliano da Sangallo and his recently deceased father Francesco, who was an architect as well as a musician. These are among the earliest portraits to characterize their sitters by profession: a pen and compass allude to architecture, the sheet music to music. Both disciplines are based on notions of harmony and proportion.

artworks.title: Portrait of Don Ramón Satué
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: outersize: height 135.5 cm (support incl. frame) x width 112 cm x depth 7 cm × support: height 107 cm x width 83.5 cm
artworks.description: Goya owes his fame to his portraits of the Spanish court and to his idiosyncratic prints. He had already turned 76 when he painted this powerful portrait. Satué was a judge in the highest tribunal of Castile. The casual pose and open collar have an informality that Goya usually reserved for portraits of his most intimate friends.

artworks.title: Selene and Endymion
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 177 cm x width 118.5 cm
artworks.description: The chaste goddess of the moon, Selene (or Diana), is in love with the shepherd Endymion. Only at night when he is asleep does she quietly creep down to him, accompanied by Cupid, whose torch symbolizes burning love. This painting was (appropriately) hung in Mary Stuart’s bedchamber in Soestdijk Palace, for Lairesse felt that the function and decoration of a room should correspond.

artworks.title: View of The Hague from the Delftse Vaart in the Seventeenth Century
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 9.5 cm × weight 54 kg × height 200 cm x width 340 cm
artworks.description: Gezicht op Den Haag, vanaf de Delftse vaart in de zeventiende eeuw. Links loopt een weg langs het water waar een molen staat en enkele wandelaars lopen, op een brug staat een man met een hengel. Rechts op het water een trekschuit. Vervaardigd ter opluistering van de feesten gehouden op 27 mei 1852 bij de gelegenheid van de onthulling van het standbeeld van Rembrandt.

artworks.title: Amsterdam City View with Houses on the Herengracht and the old Haarlemmersluis
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 44 cm x width 57.5 cm × depth 8 cm
artworks.description:
Van der Heyden captured the activity on and around the water in Amsterdam’s old town centre. With an eye
for detail, he painted the old Haarlemmersluis, a lock on the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. However, the picture
does not present a real location: Van der Heyden combined the lock with a row of houses that is actually on a different canal, the Herengracht.

artworks.title: Bluff-bowed Fishing Boat on the Beach at Scheveningen
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 14.5 cm × height 101.5 cm x width 89.5 cm x thickness 3.8 cm
artworks.description: Maris painted a bluff-bowed fishing boat at sea at least sixteen times. They are studies in light and atmosphere. To avoid the problems caused by constant- ly changing light conditions, he worked in his studio. Maris also preferred to select his colours indoors, because, as he stated, it was sometimes necessary to ‘exaggerate in order to learn about the power of colours’.

artworks.title: Portrait of Hortense de Beauharnais
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 74.7 cm x width 63.7 cm x depth 8.5 cm × height 60.9 cm x width 49.8 cm
artworks.description: Hortense de Beauharnais became the first queen of Holland in 1806 when her husband Louis Napoleon ascended the throne. In this portrait, she wears a tiara adorned with pearls, a royal jewel. However, her husband’s reign lasted for only four years, after which De Beauharnais settled on her own in Switzerland. She was a gifted musician and composer, and the cultural gatherings she organized in her home were renowned.

artworks.title: Still Life with a Silver Tazza
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, oil paint (paint), panel
artworks.dimensions: support: height 40.5 cm x width 56 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met roemer, tazza, uurwerkje, twee tinnen borden, olijven en walnoten op een gedeeltelijk bedekte tafel.

artworks.title: Time
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 9.5 cm × height 121.5 cm x width 105 cm
artworks.description: De Tijd. Vadertje Tijd, naakt en met vleugels op de rug, knielend op zijn rechterknie, in profiel naar links. Hij houdt met zijn rechterhand een doek omhoog, op de grond ligt een gouden weegschaal tussen bladeren.

artworks.title: The Denial of St Peter
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 154.5 cm x width 169.5 cm x thickness 3.6 cm
artworks.description: While Christ is being questioned by the high priests in the dead of night, Peter waits outside. A maidservant recognizes him as one of Christ’s disciples, but Peter is afraid and denies it three times. In the right background, Christ is being led away, looking back over his shoulder at Peter who has betrayed him.

artworks.title: Lioness Resting
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 40.7 cm x width 51.2 cm × depth 7.3 cm
artworks.description: Een liggende leeuwin, voor een steil oplopende achtergrond.

artworks.title: Still Life with Fruit
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, copper (metal), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 50.5 cm x width 42.5 cm × depth 7.5 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met vruchten. Op een stenen plint in het midden een tros witte druiven met perziken, pruimen, een doorgesneden granaatappel en een halve meloen. Met vlinders en andere insecten.

artworks.title: Doll’s House of Petronella Oortman
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, biological material, parchment (animal material), canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 87 cm x width 69 cm × height 99 cm x width 81.2 cm
artworks.description: This doll’s house was so expensive that a painting was made of it. In assembling a doll’s house, wealthy ladies showed the ideal version of a Dutch household. This included a Black servant, seen in the left room on the middle floor. All of the original dolls have been lost, except for a baby in a cradle.

artworks.title: Emblematic Still Life with Flagon, Glass, Jug and Bridle
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: diameter 51 cm x diameter 51.5 cm
artworks.description: A pewter flagon, a wine glass, an earthenware jug, a bridle or rein, and a piece of paper with two staves and inscribed ‘what is out of measure, perishes in immeasurable evil.’ These are exhortations to moderation. You must cut wine with water, curb your appetites. This strict message contrasts sharply with the reputation of the painter, who was repeatedly accused of whoremongery and heresy.

artworks.title: The Vegetable Garden
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 61 cm x width 87 cm × height 91 cm x width 116 cm x depth 12.5 cm
artworks.description: Mauve called himself a real ‘outdoors man’. From 1884 he regularly painted the vegetable and fruit gardens of farms. He used a bright palette instead of the greyish tones he had favoured a few years earlier. The vegetable garden here displays a wealth of green tonalities. The white accents of the linen and the woman’s cap lend depth and freshness to the image.

artworks.title: Missing Title
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 30 cm x width 53.5 cm
artworks.description: Segers incorporated elements from the Flemish landscape tradition, such as the high vantage point, rocky mountains, and thin painting technique with thicker accents. The way in which Segers rendered depth with colour and contrasts of light and dark is reminiscent of Pieter Bruegel and his followers.

artworks.title: Still Life
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: outer size: depth 10.5 cm (support incl. frame) × support: height 127 cm x width 106.5 cm x thickness 3 cm
artworks.description: Abraham van Beyeren (1620/21 - 1690). Still life, c. 1660. The Hague painter Van Beyeren has assembled a colourful assortment of objects and fruits. This type of luxurious still life was in fashion around 1650. Van Beyeren specialized in the genre, following in the footsteps of Jan Davidsz de Heem, who developed this type of still life. Purchased in 1958.

artworks.title: Lake near Loosdrecht
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), textile materials, biological material, canvas, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 30 cm x width 45 cm
artworks.description: From the inscription ‘effet de matin’, it is clear that Roelofs made this painting in the early morning. The painter devoted great attention to the shimmer-ing and sparkling of the sky and the reflective surface of the water. As he himself wrote: ‘Far more difficult than expressing the colour of the sky is to render its curvature and the vibrating play of the atmosphere.’

artworks.title: Winter Landscape
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 45 cm x width 52 cm × depth 13.5 cm
artworks.description: Witsen was an Amsterdam painter, but moved to rural Ede when he was married. He made a series of winter landscapes there. His style is characterized by subdued use of colour and a simple composition. The grey-blue sky and the snow-white field are separated by a horizontal strip with farms, violet blue trees and blue green hills. He delicately painted the treetops, possibly with a fan brush.

artworks.title: "Woman with Unicorn
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 5 cm × height 28 cm x width 39 cm
artworks.description: In een landschap zit een jonge vrouw met een eenhoorn die zijn kop in haar schoot legt. Vroeger geïnterpreteerd als de heilige Justine, als personificatie van de kuisheid en als een allegorie op de rol van de stadstaat Venetië.

artworks.title: The Departure of a Dignitary from Middelburg
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 63.2 cm x width 131.6 cm
artworks.description: All of Middelburg has turned out to watch the warship De Zeehondt is being towed out of the harbour, towards the sea, with the help of four sturdy draught horses. Someone of distinction is leaving here, because even Stadholder Maurice’s yacht takes part: it is firing a gun salute. The presence of an African child on the middle ship is notable.

artworks.title: Javanese Court Officials
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), textile materials, inorganic material, cotton (textile), paper, oil paint (paint), gilding (material)
artworks.dimensions: height 196.8 cm x width 74.3 cm × depth 4.5 cm
artworks.description: These five figures are representatives of the Javanese elite. The accurately depicted clothing and batik motifs signal where they come from and what their rank and status are. Knowledge of their etiquette and appearance was of great political importance to the colonial administration. The Javanese elite was increasingly deployed to control and exploit the colony in the first half of the 19th century.

artworks.title: The Town Hall on Dam Square, Amsterdam
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 47 cm x width 53.5 cm x depth 8 cm × height 33.5 cm x width 41.5 cm
artworks.description: The Amsterdam Town Hall (now the Royal Palace) on Dam Square counts as the most important historical and cultural monument of the 17th century in the Netherlands. The building symbolizes the tremendous growth and development the city experienced during that time. Gerrit Berckheyde here portrayed the Town Hall in all its glory while simultaneously conveying the hustle and bustle of the city’s main square.

artworks.title: Ships in a Turbulent Sea
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 159.6 cm x width 220.2 cm x thickness 4.4 cm × depth 14.4 cm × weight 53 kg
artworks.description: Schepen op een onstuimige zee. Links een oorlogsschip, op de voorgrond een Blankenbergse schuit.

artworks.title: The Lords of Montfoort
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 69.5 cm x width 142.9 cm × frame: height 86 cm x width 157.5 cm x thickness 6 cm
artworks.description: Four Dutch knights kneel before the Virgin. The first three died in 1345 in the Battle of Warns against the Frisians; the fourth was badly wounded. Behind them stands Saint George, their patron saint. The coats of arms above them show that they belong to the De Rover family of Montfoort. The painting is a ‘commemorative panel’ to honour their memory.

artworks.title: The Capture of the Royal Prince
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 6.5 cm × height 58.5 cm x width 81 cm
artworks.description: On 13 June 1666, the third day of the Four Days’ Battle, the English flagship the Royal Prince ran aground on a sandbank off the English coast. It was then captured by Cornelis Tromp, who transferred its crew to his vessel, the Gouda (at left). Admiral de Ruyter commanded Tromp to burn this prize. He would have preferred to tow it back to the Netherlands in triumph.

artworks.title: Meadow Landscape with Cattle
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 49.2 cm x width 77.3 cm × height 83 cm x width 113 cm x depth 13 cm
artworks.description: Unlike Romantic painters, Hague School artists had an eye for the beauty of the polder landscape. Instead of the dramatic and varied landscapes of the Romantic tradition, they painted cows ruminating tranquilly in verdant meadows with a panoramic horizon. These works were greatly appreciated and gave rise to the image of the Netherlands as a green, flat polder landscape under a greyish blue sky.

artworks.title: Interior of an inn with an old man amusing himself with the landlady and two men playing backgammon, known as 'Two kinds of games'
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 63 cm x width 69.5 cm × depth 7.5 cm
artworks.description: Herberginterieur met een oude man, die zich vergrijpt aan de waardin. Daarachter enkele triktrakspelers en een drinkende man. De voorstelling staat bekend als 'Tweeërlei spel'. Links een grote haard waarboven takken zijn gehangen, aan de muur een luit. Op de vloer ligt een hond naast een omgevallen kruk tussen eierschalen en mosselen.

artworks.title: Orchard
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 55 cm x width 107.5 cm × depth 16.5 cm
artworks.description: Een boomgaard met fruitbomen in bloei.

artworks.title: Vrouwen aan zee
artworks.medium: paper, paint (coating), pasteboard, cardboard, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 36 cm x width 46 cm
artworks.description: Vrouwen aan zee. Twee vrouwen lopen met een kind op de arm over duinen langs de zee.

artworks.title: The Dutch Raid on the Medway, 1667
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: outer size: depth 6.5 cm (support incl. frame) × support: height 72.4 cm x width 107.3 cm
artworks.description: Het verbranden van de Engelse vloot op de rivier de Medway bij Chatham, 20 juni 1667. Episode uit de Tweede Engelse Oorlog. Nederlandse en Engelse oorlogsschepen op zee, in het midden het vlaggeschip The Royal Charles. Tussen de brandende schepen varen meerdere sloepen.

artworks.title: Salome with the Head of John the Baptist
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: frame: height 83.8 cm x width 66.5 cm x thickness 5.5 cm × support: height 71.8 cm x width 53.6 cm
artworks.description: Salome danced seductively for King Herod, and, as a reward, she was granted a wish. Urged on by her mother Herodias, Salome asked for the head of John the Baptist, who had criticized Herodias’ adultery with the king. Salome is showing us her prize, the saint’s head on a platter.

artworks.title: View of The Hague
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 10 cm × height 48 cm x width 58 cm
artworks.description: In the 19th century Rembrandt grew into the national hero of the Netherlands. In Amsterdam a statue was erected in his honour. For its ceremonial unveiling, the Parkzaal (a concert hall) was decorated with huge paintings of towns where he was thought to have worked. This is the sketch for the canvas Rembrandt in The Hague. In the distance one sees the silhouette of the city with the church tower of the Grote or Sint- Jacobskerk. Only later did it emerge that Rembrandt had never actually worked in The Hague.

artworks.title: Prince’s Day
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 46 cm x width 62.5 cm
artworks.description:
Prince’s Day! This popular feast-day celebrated the birthday (14 November 1650) of Prince William III of
Orange-Nassau. How this was done is explained on the piece of paper on the floor in the middle foreground.
This translates as: ‘To the health of the Nassau laddie, in one hand a rapier, and in the other a glass raised gladly.’ This is sure to boost spirits; the revellers take no notice of the portrait of the prince ‘overlooking’ the scene.

artworks.title: Still Life with Vegetables before a Draped, Overturned Plinth by an Ornamental Fountain
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, copper (metal), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 38.4 cm x width 47.5 cm × outer size: depth 4.5 cm (support incl. frame)
artworks.description: Stilleven van bloemen, vruchten en vaatwerk bij een fontein met een putto op een dolfijn, tussen zuilen. Linksonder twee hazen, een bloemkool en een kalebas, druiven, maïs, abrikozen, appels en aalbessen. Rechts een gouden lampetstel en een aapje (meerkat). Tussen de vruchten zitten allerlei vogeltjes, vlinders en andere insecten.

artworks.title: Landscape with Bathsheba
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 100.4 cm x width 203.9 cm × frame: height 222.8 cm x width 121 cm x thickness 6.5 cm
artworks.description: Everything here exudes Classical antiquity, from the ancient fountain statues to the Classical architecture of the palace. The biblical story is subordinate to the vast panorama. Bathsheba sits bathing at lower left and is being spied on by King David, the small figure on the balcony at upper right. Even from that distance, he is seduced by Bathsheba’s beauty.

artworks.title: The Egg Dance
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 84 cm x width 172 cm × weight 20.5 kg
artworks.description: At right, in this brothel, a young man does an egg dance to the music of a bagpiper. While dancing, he had to roll an egg within a chalk circle – without it breaking – and to cover it with a wooden bowl. This ‘pointless’ amusement, along with the dissolute behaviour of the other figures, served as a moral warning against debauchery.

artworks.title: Still Life with Fruit
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 60 cm x width 45.5 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met vruchten. Op de hoek van een tafel staat een tinnen bord waarop een geschilde citroen en een tak met kersen liggen, daarachter een Chinese kom met druiven, een vijg, perziken en pruimen.

artworks.title: The First Day of School
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 38.5 cm x width 53 cm × weight 2.6 kg
artworks.description: A mother, accompanied by a group of women, brings her daughter to school for the first time. That the women are Turkish can be seen from their colourful clothing and the yellow slippers that only Muslims could wear, according to sumptuary laws (dress codes). A servant carries the girl’s embroidery frame. Needlework was a favourite pastime of women in affluent Turkish circles. Women held in slavery did the household chores.

artworks.title: Plantation in Surinam
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 52.5 cm x width 45.5 cm × height 67 cm x width 59.4 cm x depth 4 cm
artworks.description: Jonas Witsen inherited the Waterland, Surimombo, and Palmeneribo plantations from his wife Sara Scharphuijzen. He sent the painter Dirk Valkenburg to Surinam to inspect these sites. In the foreground of the painting are some Lokono, among the original inhabitants of this region. The many people who worked in slavery on the plantation are missing in this representation.

artworks.title: Interior with a Woman Feeding a Parrot, Known as ‘The Parrot Cage’
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), textile materials, biological material, canvas, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 50 cm x width 40 cm
artworks.description: This scene bursts with life. On the left, a woman is frying oysters, while a mischievous boy tries to feed a cat. On the right, two men are playing a game of trictrac (a kind of backgammon). Through his use of colour, Steen directed attention to the woman in the middle giving a parrot a biscuit. Thanks to the light falling on her and her green and violet gown, she stands out against the other, more drably painted figures.

artworks.title: Prometheus Being Chained by Vulcan
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 201 cm x width 182 cm
artworks.description:
Prometheus stole fire from the gods and gave it to mankind. As punishment, Vulcan chained him to a rock, where an eagle pecked out his liver causing him excruciating pain. Here we see Prometheus being chained, his face contorted with fear, while Mercury laughs at him. Van Baburen borrowed the dramatic illumination and the figure’s sunburned hands and faces from
his great model Caravaggio.

artworks.title: Portrait of Lizzy Ansingh
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 78 cm x width 62 cm × depth 9.5 cm
artworks.description: Thérèse Schwartze was the most sought-after portraitist of Dutch 19th-century high society. Yet the portraits she painted of those closest to her were her favourites. This likeness of her niece and fellow artist Lizzy Ansingh is one of her best works. The strong contrast between light and dark creates an intimate atmosphere. At the same time, the energetic brushwork and fiery red accent on the bright green in her clothes exude a powerful aura.

artworks.title: Bentheim Castle
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 68 cm x width 54 cm
artworks.description: Bentheim Castle still exists. It is located on the German–Dutch border region, but the high mountains Ruisdael depicted in this painting are not found there. Fantasy and reality are interwoven in this scene. The painter made a dozen paintings of this castle, each with a different mountain landscape. In 1861, Goethe, the famous German writer, rightly called Ruisdael a poet.

artworks.title: Still Life with Quinces, Medlars and a Glass
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 5.5 cm × height 41.5 cm x width 34.5 cm
artworks.description: Virtually nothing is known about the painter Martinus Nellius, only a few works by whom have been preserved. He must have been active in Leiden and The Hague and, like his contemporary Adriaen Coorte, specialized in still lifes with simple compositions featuring only a few objects  or fruits rendered with a great eye for detail.

artworks.title: A Market Stall in Batavia
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: outer size: depth 5 cm (support incl. frame) × support: height 106 cm x width 175.5 cm × total: weight 19 kg
artworks.description: A Chinese merchant in Batavia (present-day Jakarta on Java, Indonesia) offers a wide variety of fruit in his stall. He sells rambutan, mangosteen, durian, copra, mango, grapefruit, pineapple and banana. A woman buys betel nuts for chewing wrapped in a sirih (betel) leaf. The large Chinese community played an important role in Batavia. Chinese were primarily active as merchants and craftsmen.

artworks.title: "Council of War aboard ""The Seven Provinces"", the Flagship of Michiel Adriaenszoon de Ruyter, 10 June 1666, preceding the Four Days' Battle: episode from the Second Anglo-Dutch War"
artworks.medium: textile materials, materials by function, canvas, ink
artworks.dimensions: depth 8.5 cm × height 117 cm x width 175 cm
artworks.description: Council of War on the Zeven Provinciën, 10 June 1666. By Willem van de Velde I, 1666. On board Michiel de Ruyter's flagship (right) the commanders of the Dutch warships meet for a council of war. The signal for the gathering is the white flag on the stern. The flag and pennant on the main mast indicate that this is the admiral's ship. The council took place on 10 June 1666, the eve of the Four Days Fight, a major engagement of the Second Anglo-Dutch War against a combined French and English fleet. Willem van de Velde specialised in maritime pen paintings. To be able to portray this battle he sailed for a period with De Ruyter's fleet.

artworks.title: Portrait of Haesje Jacobsdr van Cleyburg
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 68.6 cm x width 53.4 cm
artworks.description: Rembrandt travelled to Rotterdam to portray the brewing couple Haesje van Cleyburg and Dirck Pesser, who were part of the city’s Remonstrant elite. While at first glance her attire may seem modest, in reality it was quite lavish. The millstone collar around her neck was a very expensive accessory, requiring as much as fifteen metres of fabric.

artworks.title: Vanitas Still Life with Books
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, biological material, panel
artworks.dimensions: height 73.5 cm x width 70 cm
artworks.description: Vanitas stilleven met boeken. Stapels van boeken met een schedel, een kaars, enkele documenten met zegels, een inktpot met pen en een liedboek op een tafel.

artworks.title: View in the Woods
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 9.5 cm × weight 7 kg × height 46 cm x width 38 cm
artworks.description: Bosgezicht. Kraaien scharrelen op de grond tussen hoge smalle bomen.

artworks.title: Javanese Court Officials
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), textile materials, inorganic material, cotton (textile), paper, oil paint (paint), gilding (material)
artworks.dimensions: height 196.8 cm x width 74.3 cm × depth 4.5 cm
artworks.description: These five figures are representatives of the Javanese elite. The accurately depicted clothing and batik motifs signal where they come from and what their rank and status are. Knowledge of their etiquette and appearance was of great political importance to the colonial administration. The Javanese elite was increasingly deployed to control and exploit the colony in the first half of the 19th century.

artworks.title: The Death of the Pharaoh’s Firstborn Son
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 77 cm x width 124.5 cm
artworks.description: In this scene from the biblical book of Exodus, Moses and Aaron (upper right) visit the pharaoh, who is mourning his son. The Egyptian ruler’s son had died from one of the plagues sent by God to secure the Israelites’ release from Egypt. The gloom of the painting reflects the father’s intense grief. One has to look long and hard to discern all the figures and details.

artworks.title: 'Isabella'
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 41 cm x width 29 cm × depth 11 cm
artworks.description: In creating this portrait, Maris first took photographs of the young girl as reference material. Thanks to those pictures and other documents in Maris’ archive, we know the girl was about twelve years old when she posed for him. Maris made several portraits of her, some bearing the title Isabella, including this painting. This was possibly not her real name, as models commonly used aliases.

artworks.title: View in Bentheim Forest
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 84 cm x width 119 cm × depth 11.5 cm
artworks.description: This landscape is clearly constructed and painted in detail. You can see everything very distinctly: the ground, the trees, the sky. The light falls in such a way that two elements stand out: the majestic tree on the left, and the woodworkers on the right. The people are tiny next to nature itself, presented here as larger and stronger than them.

artworks.title: Portrait of Louis Napoleon, King of Holland
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 223 cm x width 147 cm
artworks.description: In 1795 French troops invaded the Netherlands. The country became an ally of France and enjoyed a large degree of independence, until 1806 when Napoleon seized power and made his brother Louis Napoleon King of Holland. Louis showed sympathy for his new kingdom and supported Dutch interests. This had not been Napoleon’s intention and in 1810 he forced his brother to abdicate.

artworks.title: Witches' Sabbath
artworks.artist: Claes Jacobsz van der Heck (signed by artist)
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 56.8 cm x width 97.9 cm
artworks.description: Heksensabbat. Fantasielandschap met antieke gebouwen en ruïnes waartussen zich allerlei monsters en gedrochten bevinden. Ook vliegen duivels en heksen door de lucht. Rechts een fontein, in het midden een obelisk en een beeld van een dikke duivel zittend op een wereldbol, links een open bouwwerk waarin beneden een gezelschap rond een tafel zit en boven monsters koken in een grote ketel.

artworks.title: Rue Notre-Dame, Paris
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 58.5 cm x width 67 cm x thickness 7 cm × height 38.7 cm x width 47.6 cm
artworks.description: After having gained a reputation with his harbour scenes along the coast of Normandy, Jongkind turned in the summer of 1866 to other subject matter – the reconstruction and expansion of Paris. In this street scene, he concentrated on the play of brilliant sunlight and powerful shadows, using light tints and swift, loose brushstrokes. This new, sunny tonality and modern subject matter were later taken up by the Impressionists.

artworks.title: Captured English Ships after the Four Days’ Battle
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 58 cm x width 81 cm × depth 7.5 cm
artworks.description: Battered English and Dutch ships lie in Goeree Gat after the indecisive engagement known as the Four Days’ Battle (11–14 June 1666). In the foreground is the captured warship the Swiftsure, with the English royal arms on its counter. Its bowsprit, foremast and main mast have been splintered by cannon fire; the English flag droops off its stern. At the far right is the Hollandia, the heavily damaged ship of Cornelis Tromp.

artworks.title: Portrait of Willem III (1650-1702), Prince of Orange, as a Child
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 133 cm x width 94 cm × outer size: depth 7 cm (support incl. frame) × weight 19 kg
artworks.description: Portret van Willem III, prins van Oranje, als kind. Staand, ten voeten uit, bij een oranjeboom in een pot, met een oranjeappel in de rechterhand. Bij zijn voeten en springend hondje. Op het hoofd een zwarte baret versierd met struisvogelveren en een juwelenband.

artworks.title: A Dutch Girl at Breakfast
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 46.8 cm x width 39 cm
artworks.description: A young woman, the painter’s wife, drinks coffee, a popular beverage in the 18th century. In 1775, the magazine De Vaderlander called (in vain) for a coffee boycott: ‘Unfortunate calloused fists had to work the ground for the coffee and sugar that you now hold in your delicate little hands. They were murdered to meet your needs.’

artworks.title: 'The Joy of Motherhood'
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 106 cm x width 129 cm × depth 10 cm
artworks.description: Voorstelling getiteld 'Moederweelde'. In een interieur zit een jonge moeder aan een tafel bij het raam kleding te verstellen. Op haar schoot een slapend kind, bij haar knieën staat een jongetje te kijken naar enkele over de vloer scharrelende kippen. Door het venster is in de verte een dorp te zien.

artworks.title: Dutch Ships Ramming Spanish Galleys near Calais, 3 October 1602
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 118 cm x width 151 cm × outer size: depth 6.5 cm (support incl. frame)
artworks.description: Terror emanates from the bald-shaven and half-naked galley slaves. While the soldiers aboard still have a chance to escape, the enslaved crew remains chained to the rowing benches, condemned to face death by drowning. The Dutch revolt against Spain unfolded primarily at sea, where the Spanish galleys proved powerless against the robust Dutch three-masters that simply rammed into them.

artworks.title: The Sick Woman
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 76 cm x width 63.5 cm
artworks.description: Faint from fever, the young woman rests her head on a pillow. Is she perhaps lovesick? Is she pregnant? To find out, a quack would put a strip of his patient’s clothing in a brazier to smoulder – the scent would disclose her secret. Jan Steen here presents such a charlatan making a diagnosis. His old-fashioned attire characterizes him as a comic character.

artworks.title: Winter Scene
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 133 cm x width 191 cm × depth 9 cm
artworks.description: Wintergezicht. Landschap met sneeuw en ijs. Bevroren vaart buiten een dorp, links een kerk, rechts enkele molens op een dijk. Op het ijs wordt geschaatst en lopen enkele figuren met sledes. Links een stalletje waar een vlag buiten hangt.

artworks.title: Still Life with Fruit, Plates and Dishes on a Turkey Carpet
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 9 cm × height 128.5 cm x width 136 cm x thickness 3.7 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met vruchten en vaatwerk op een Smyrna kleed. Op een tafel bedekt met een Oosters tapijt liggen een Wan Li-schaal met appels en citroenen, zilveren schalen, een gouden pronkbeker, een brood op een tinnen bord, een roemer met wijn waarin een geschilde citroen hangt, verder druiven en een peer. Achteraan staat een grote porseleinen vaas of pot.

artworks.title: Venus and Adonis
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 135 cm x width 109 cm
artworks.description:
Venus, the goddess of love, warns her lover Adonis of the danger of the hunt. In vain, however, for he is killed by a wild boar. On the left, Cupid, the god of love, already gestures in despair. The tall, slender figures with small heads are characteristic of Spranger’s
style. The hilly landscape is ‘old-fashioned’: the artist derived it from an early 16th-century painting.

artworks.title: Rough Sea with a Dutch Yacht
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 8 cm × height 37 cm x width 46 cm
artworks.description: Originally from Emden in Germany, Ludolf Bakhuysen specialized in marine painting in Amsterdam. In this seascape he depicted various types of ships sailing on choppy water and under a dramatic cloudy sky. At the right is a yacht with a grand showing of the flag. Bakhuysen placed his signature on the fluttering flag. In the left foreground is a fisherman pulling his nets into a little boat. In the background is a warship lying at anchor that has just fired a salute.

artworks.title: Bos met berkebomen
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 41 cm x width 31.3 cm x thickness 3 cm × depth 5.3 cm
artworks.description: Gezicht in een open bos met berken.

artworks.title: The Adoration of the Magi
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: painted surface: height 89.2 cm x width 69.2 cm × support: height 91.6 cm x width 71.8 cm
artworks.description: The painter Geertgen tot Sint-Jans lived in Haarlem in the monastery of the Sint-Jansheren (the Commandery of the Knights of Saint John), from which he took his name.The three magi represent the three generations and hail from the three continents known in the Middle Ages: Europe, Asia and Africa. They are paying tribute to the newborn baby Jesus.

artworks.title: View of the Church of Sloten in the Winter
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 11 cm × height 90 cm x width 128 cm
artworks.description: Gezicht op de kerk van Sloten in de winter, met op het ijs schaatsers en kolfspelers. Rechts gaat langs enige woningen en over twee bruggen de Osdorperweg, die bij de kerk uitkomt op de Sloterweg.

artworks.title: Portrait of a Woman
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 8 cm × height 46 cm x width 36 cm
artworks.description: Portret van een vrouw. Buste met bloemen in het haar en op de borst.

artworks.title: Vanitas Still Life
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 7.5 cm × height 102.5 cm x width 132 cm
artworks.description: Vanitas stilleven. Op een tafel naast een zuil liggen verschillende boeken, reisverslagen en wetenschappelijke verhandelingen, sommige opengeslagen, een aardglobe en een hemelglobe, een geldbuidel, een kroon, decoratietekens, een horloge en een pronkbeker.

artworks.title: David Leeuw and Cornelia Hooft with their Children
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 190 cm x width 200 cm
artworks.description: The affluent Mennonite Leeuw-Hooft family is portrayed here making music; even the youngest daughter, Suzanna, joins in holding her flute. They are performing a religious song, with both the notes and lyrics clearly legible. Singing and music held great importance in the practice of their faith. Together, they embody a harmonious family life. The interplay of the sitters’ hands underscores the bond uniting them.

artworks.title: The Crucifixion
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 105 cm x width 88.4 cm x height 105 cm x width 86.5 cm
artworks.description: For his depiction of Golgotha, the mountain on which Christ was crucified, the artist chose a high viewpoint. In doing so, he created a vast landscape in which to represent successive episodes of the Passion of Christ simultaneously. This narrative convention was often used in medieval painting.

artworks.title: Still Life wit Flowers
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 4.5 cm × height 116 cm x width 64 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met bloemen. Boeket met stokrozen in een pot staande op een tafel.

artworks.title: View in a Forest, outer right wing of a triptych
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: frame: height 98 cm x width 39 cm × sight size: height 88.5 cm x width 29.2 cm × support: height 89.8 cm x width 30.8 cm
artworks.description: Bosgezicht. Eén van de twee bosgezichten op de buitenzijde van de twee zijpanelen van een drieluik (zie ook SK-A-3134). Het betreft hier het rechterzijpaneel met een os en een ezel bij het water. De binnenzijden van deze zijpanelen en het middenpaneel (met een aanbidding van het kind) bevinden zich in het Metropolitan Musuem of Art in New York.

artworks.title: Portrait of William II, King of the Netherlands
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 109.5 cm x width 86 cm
artworks.description: This is a portrait of King William II in military uniform, but with a decidedly informal air. Accompanied by his hound, he poses casually in the dunes, which in the Romantic era was considered the quintessentially Dutch landscape. In 1848 –when revolutions were raging throughout Europe –William II renounced royal autocracy and the Netherlands became a parliamentary democracy.

artworks.title: Still Life with Game and a Greek Stele: Allegory of Autumn
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 146 cm x width 116 cm
artworks.description: Dead animals, a gun and a powder horn: everything in this still life relates to hunting. The Greek marble stele (memorial tablet) in the background presents a huntress (the goddess Diana?), and the bronze relief in the foreground depicts putti hunting. The pendant of this painting (next to it) also includes a relief, that one showing Venus, the goddess of love, making her toilet.

artworks.title: Encounter during the Battle of Kijkduin
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 114 cm x width 183 cm
artworks.description:
This painting is traditionally called the Nocturnal Battle. However, the naval battle at Kijkduin, between Cornelis Tromp on the Gouden Leeuw and Sir Edward Spragg on the Royal Prince, actually took place in daylight hours on 21 August 1673. It looks like night only because the encounter is shown partially hidden behind clouds of smoke and gunpowder fumes. While the Dutch flagship is sinking at the right, Tromp
battles on from a captured ship.

artworks.title: Birds in a Park
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 112 cm x width 140 cm × weight 21.6 kg
artworks.description: Vogels in een park. Op de voorgrond twee hanen en een kip met haar kuikens. Links in een boom zit een hop, een duif komt aangevlogen. Rechts een pauw en in het verschiet nog een pauw, een kalkoen en een zwaan.

artworks.title: Still Life
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 82 cm x width 60 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven op de hoek van een tafel: tinnen schenkkan en borden met een geschilde citroen, mes en olijven, een berkenmeier met wijn en een zilveren pronkbeker.

artworks.title: Paarden bij het hek
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 9.9 cm × height 42.8 cm x width 25.3 cm × weight 6 kg
artworks.description: Landschap. Drie paarden staan bij het hek bij een slootje. Links een rij hoge bomen.

artworks.title: Storm in the Strait of Dover
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 7 cm × height 65 cm x width 88 cm
artworks.description: Storm in het Nauw van Calais. Schepen op zee nabij een kust tijdens een storm.

artworks.title: Winter
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: frame: height 44 cm x width 44.5 cm x depth 5.5 cm × support: diameter 33.4 cm
artworks.description: This winter scene accompanies a summer landscape on view elsewhere in this gallery. When Van Goyen painted the two little pictures in 1625, he rested on a long tradition. As early as the Middle Ages, artists portrayed the seasons by means of landscapes with people engaged in typical  seasonal activities.

artworks.title: Bloemen
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 4 cm × height 91 cm x width 48 cm
artworks.description: Schets van een boeket bloemen.

artworks.title: The Great Assembly of 1651
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, inorganic material, panel, metal, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 52 cm x width 66 cm
artworks.description:
This is the Ridderzaal (Hall of Knights) at the Binnenhof in The Hague. Hanging from the ceiling are Southern Netherlandish and Spanish flags captured during the war. The representatives of the seven provinces of the Dutch Republic are gathered in the hall. When Stadholder William II, son of Frederick Henry, dies at the end of 1650, most of the provinces decide after lengthy deliberations not to appoint a new stadholder on 21
August 1651. The war is over, and – as they concur – the country is more than able to face the future without the Oranges.

artworks.title: Pierre de Moucheron (1508-67), his Wife Isabeau de Gerbier, their eighteen Children, their Son-in-Law Allard de la Dale and their first Grandchild
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: weight 30 kg × depth 6 cm × height 108 cm x width 246 cm
artworks.description: The De Moucheron Family. Antwerp school, 1563. Pierre de Moucheron (1508-1567) and his wife Isabeau de Gerbier are surrounded by their children and grandchildren. Beside Pierre: his son-in-law and sons - oldest to youngest. The daughters are standing beside their mother, also oldest to youngest. Their ages are written above their heads. Pierre de Moucheron and his equally enterprising sons were active at the start of the Dutch Golden Age. Pierre founded a dynasty of Protestant merchants and ship owners. He ran a trading company in Antwerp. When the city fell to Spain in 1585, the firm moved to Middelburg. The towns of Zeeland and Holland profited immensely from the influx of wealthy refugees from the Southern Netherlands.

artworks.title: The Shop of the Bookdealer Pieter Meijer Warnars on the Vijgendam in Amsterdam
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 48 cm x width 58 cm
artworks.description: Amsterdam’s cultural elite met up in this book and print shop. Warnars, the owner, was a bookdealer, publisher and printer. These activities are reflected in the full bookcases, the hanging banner, new reams of paper and the printing press on the floor. The painter of this scene, Johannes Jelgerhuis, was also a noted actor. The pronounced perspective of the shop interior makes it look like a stage set with a city view as a backdrop.

artworks.title: Vanitas Still Life
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 9.3 cm x width 12 cm × height 13.7 cm x width 16.6 cm x depth 1.6 cm
artworks.description: Vanitas stilleven. Op een tafel staan en liggen enkele boeken en paperassen. In het midden een schedel en een zandloper.

artworks.title: Stilleven met kan van steengoed
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 6.2 cm × height 78.5 cm x width 58 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met gedecoreerde kan van steengoed, twee bossen asperges, enkele citroenen, een fles, een koperen wijnkoeler met flessen en wijnranken en een blad papier.

artworks.title: Dutch Ships in the Roads of Texel; in the middle the 'Gouden Leeuw',  the Flagship of Cornelis Tromp
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 92 cm x width 140 cm × depth 7.5 cm
artworks.description: Marines embarking on the Texel roads by Ludolf Bakhuysen, 1671. Large ships sailed from the harbours of the Zuiderzee to Texel with a minimal crew and provisions. At Texel they took on water and victuals, and here the sailors, soldiers and officers embarked. A unit of marines led by their commander on the beach is marching towards the harbour pier. Boats are ready to ferry them to the warships. A high-ranking officer and his wife are watching the activity from a low dune. He is wearing a gold-embroidered sash with sword and is pointing out the ships lying at anchor with his walkingstick. In 1665 Baron Joseph van Gendt was given command of the marine company. Perhaps this is the man with the walkingstick.

artworks.title: Landscape
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 10 cm × height 57.2 cm x width 82.4 cm x thickness 4 cm
artworks.description: Landschap. Een herder met vee arriveert bij zonsondergang bij een rivier.

artworks.title: Still Life with Passionflowers
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 41.5 cm x width 33.5 cm × depth 7.5 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met passiebloemen en passievruchten, waarbij ook een hagedis en een slak.

artworks.title: 'Sunny Day', a Windmill on a Waterway
artworks.artist: Paul Joseph Constantin Gabriël (mentioned on object)
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 10 cm × height 29 cm x width 37.5 cm
artworks.description: 'Zonnige dag'. Landschap met een molen bij het water op de voorgrond. Links een man met een hengel bij een schuurtje, rechts riet.

artworks.title: Winter in the Scheveningen Woods
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 48.5 cm x width 33 cm × depth 9.5 cm
artworks.description: With the invention of modern painting materials, such as the paint tube, working out of doors became much easier. For the first time, artists ainted directly what they saw before them. They focused on details such as the reflection of light in water, and on natural elements like sand and snow. Here Mauve presents a wood gatherer at work, but seems particularly fascinated by the texture and colour of snow and wintery trees.

artworks.title: A Writer Trimming his Pen
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 27.5 cm x width 23.5 cm
artworks.description: While studying in Paris as a young man, Ekels came to appreciate 17th-century Dutch masters – such as Metsu and Ter Borch – who specialized in interior scenes with one or more figures. He made this painting, an example of this genre, upon returning to his native Amsterdam. Ekels probably never saw any work by Vermeer, but his use of light recalls the master’s style.

artworks.title: Landscape with Fruits and Vegetables in the foreground
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 39 cm x width 50 cm × depth 5.5 cm
artworks.description: Landschap met groenten en vruchten. Op de voorgrond groeien onder een knoestige boom pompoenen of kalebassen, kolen en artisjokken. Links rust een man onder een boom, in de verte een boerderij.

artworks.title: The Drunken Couple
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), hardwood, biological material, oil paint (paint), oak (wood)
artworks.dimensions: height 52.5 cm x width 64 cm
artworks.description: A man and woman are so drunk that they are unaware they are being robbed. Their foolishness is underscored by the print on the partition. It depicts an owl, considered a stupid creature in the 17th century. After all, it could not see by day, not even with a candle or eyeglasses. The drunken couple is thus just as blind as the owl, a message that survives in the English idiom ‘blind as a bat’.

artworks.title: The Trading Post of the Dutch East India Company in Hooghly, Bengal
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 203 cm x width 313 cm
artworks.description: There is much activity in and around the fort at the trading post in Hougly, Bengal (northeast India): ships of the Dutch East India Company (VOC) sail along the Ganges River, the director visits an Indian ruler and enslaved people are at work. In the 17th century Bengal was one of the places where the VOC and its employees bought the most people. They transported them to other VOC trading posts around the Indian ocean.

artworks.title: The Cattle Ferry
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 75.5 cm x width 113 cm
artworks.description:
This painting is a milestone, for never before had a Dutch painter depicted his native flat, watery landscape
in such a monumental format. Dusk is falling, and the light is beginning to fade. The glistening river winds its way into the distance, drawing the viewer along, too, past countless little figures.

artworks.title: Jewish Wedding
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 137 cm x width 148 cm
artworks.description: Een joodse bruiloft. Het bruidspaar staat onder het gebedskleed, de bruidegom schuift de ring om de vinger van zijn bruid. Links een oude man met hoge hoed bij een brandende kaars, om het paar heen staan de bruiloftsgasten.

artworks.title: Still Life
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 153 cm x width 166 cm × depth 7 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met muziekinstrumenten, vaatwerk en fruit. Links een cister, een luit, een cello, een viool, een doedelzak, een trompet of hoorn, een fluit en bladmuziek. Op tafel liggen verschillende bokalen, schalen en borden. In een mand fruit, waaronder druiven, citroenen, een meloen, appels en peren.

artworks.title: Young Woman in Fantasy Costume
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 65 cm x width 48 cm × height 86.8 cm x width 70.5 cm x depth 6.5 cm
artworks.description: The young woman’s clothing is not in keeping with the fashions of Rembrandt’s day, but rather reflects styles of earlier centuries. The woman’s distinctive features – a domed forehead, slightly bulging eyes, and pronounced chin – are easily recognized in depictions of ancient goddesses and heroines that Rembrandt painted in the 1630s. Thus the painting is not strictly a portrait, but a ‘tronie’, or fantasy head.

artworks.title: The Virgin and Child with Four Holy Virgins
artworks.artist: Master of the Virgo inter Virgines
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 123.1 cm x width 101.1 cm
artworks.description: This painting is an ode to chastity. The Virgin sits in an enclosed garden, a symbol of virginity, surrounded by four other virgins (‘virgo inter virgines’). From attributes on their necklaces, they are identifiable as Saint Catherine with a wheel and sword, Saint Cecilia with an organ, Saint Barbara with a tower and Saint Ursula with a heart and arrow.

artworks.title: Shells on a Stone Plinth
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, oil paint (paint), paper, panel
artworks.dimensions: height 29 cm x width 22.5 cm × height 0 cm x width 0 cm
artworks.description: Coorte arranged the shells on a stone plinth against a dark background in such a way that each one receives attention, displaying its own form, colour, and structure. Coorte, moreover, painted them life size. These kinds of exotic shells were brought to the Netherlands in the ships of the Dutch East and West India Companies and were highly prized by collectors, who paid enormous amounts for them.

artworks.title: Memorial Portrait of Moses ter Borch
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 76.2 cm x width 56.5 cm
artworks.description: Moses died in 1667 during the storming of Fort Languard near Felixstowe in England. Not long thereafter Gerard and Gesina painted this picture in memory of their youngest brother. Gerard painted Moses’ portrait, Gesina the background and the objects. These allude to Moses’ heroic death and the transience of life, such as time (the pocket watch), death (the skull), eternity (ivy on the rocks) and loyalty (the dogs).

artworks.title: View of the Coffee Plantation Marienbosch in Surinam
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 75 cm x width 97.5 cm
artworks.description: Gezicht op de koffieplantage Marienbosch aan de Commewijnerivier. Tussen twee groepen palmbomen en een waterwerk (loossluis) liggen aan de overzijde van een kanaal verschillende houten plantagegebouwen. Op een stenen vloer tussen de gebouwen verspreiden tot slaaf gemaakte mensen van Afrikaanse oorsprong koffiebonen zodat deze in de zon kunnen drogen. Naast koffie werd er ook katoen en cacao op Marienbosch verbouwd. Op het kanaal vaart een korjaal, een kleine vrachtboot. Op het pad langs het kanaal loopt een tot slaafgemaakte vrouw met kind en een man met hoed en wandelstok. Volgens het opschrift rechtsonder is het schilderij vervaardigd naar een tekening van A.L. Brockmann.

artworks.title: Still Life with Fruit
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 84 cm x width 66 cm × depth 5.5 cm
artworks.description: Stilleven met vruchten. Op een marmeren plint een stilleven met ananas, maïs, druiven, peren, bessen, hazelnoten, sinaasappels, abrikozen, een meloen, bramen en pruimen. Daarnaast zijn ook enkele bloemen, takken met bladeren en vlinders aanwezig. Rechts een vaas met putti.

artworks.title: Man Smoking a Pipe
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 48 cm x width 36.6 cm x width 37 cm × height 64 cm x width 52.8 cm x thickness 6.5 cm
artworks.description: A young man leans on a window ledge, smoking a pipe and looking out at us. Dou was a master of illusionism. The open book on the sill seems to protrude from the window into our space, and the green curtain hanging from the copper rod is so realistically painted that we are tempted to draw it farther back. However, the painting’s small size gives away the deception.

artworks.title: The Hut
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 76 cm x width 65 cm
artworks.description: In composing this scene, Van de Velde relied on various preliminary drawings made from life. His superb skills as a painter of figures and animals were renowned in the 17th century, and he was regularly asked to paint the staffage in the landscapes and city views of other artists.

artworks.title: A Service in the Geertekerk, Utrecht
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 10.5 cm × height 91.5 cm x width 114.5 cm
artworks.description: Interieur van de Geertekerk te Utrecht met de viering van het heillig avondmaal.

artworks.title: Girl at the Piano
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 9.5 cm × height 37.1 cm x width 22.3 cm x depth 3.2 cm
artworks.description: Een meisje spelend aan de piano, gezien van opzij. Boven de piano hangt een schilderij.

artworks.title: Portrait of Maria van Strijp
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 98 cm x width 76 cm × outer size: depth 5.5 cm (support incl. SK-L-3165)
artworks.description: Maria van Strijp was a member of a wealthy Haarlem family active in the flourishing textile trade. Her jewellery and black dress sumptuously trimmed with lace are far more valuable than this painting of her. The decision to commission Verspronck for her portrait was easily made: he was the specialist in capturing luxurious fabrics and jewels.

artworks.title: The Holy Family at Night
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), hardwood, biological material, mahogany (wood), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 66.5 cm x width 78 cm
artworks.description:
De schaduw van zijn grootmoeder torent uit boven het vredig slapende kindje Jezus. Zijn moeder leest rustig ene boek. Het intieme huiselijke tafereel wordt slechts door een enkele lichtbron belicht.
Dit thema werd in de jaren 1640 vaker uitgebeeld in Rembrandts atelier. Het sterke licht-donkercontrast is typerend voor de meester. Toch is dit schilderij niet van zijn hand. Het werd waarschijnlijk door een van zijn leerlingen geschilderd.

artworks.title: Landschap
