artworks.title: The Flagellation
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, biological material, panel
artworks.dimensions: height 39 cm x width 30 cm
artworks.description: Like many small paintings of the period, this came from a series of predella panels formerly on the base of a large altarpiece. Such panels often showed the Virgin and Child accompanied by a few standing saints. Sometimes, however, artists had more freedom in the choice and handling of predella scenes, while the main altarpiece itself was usually fairly conventional.

artworks.title: The Defeated Spanish Garrison Leaving 's-Hertogenbosch, 17 September 1629
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 109 cm x width 173 cm
artworks.description: The defeated Spanish garrison leaving Den Bosch, 17 September 1629, by Pauwels van Hillegaert, c. 1630. Soldiers, Catholic priests and a long line of wagons are leaving Den Bosch. Some have already passed the town's outer defences. The siege lasted four months before the Spaniards were forced to open the gates to Frederick Henry. By capturing Den Bosch - strategically located in the south of the Republic - the Dutch guaranteed the security of their state. For the Catholics of Brabant, however, it represented the start of a period of repression.

artworks.description: Tischbein came from a German family of artists and was called the ‘Dutch Tischbein’. His elegant likenesses were universally admired.

artworks.description: A herder drives his cattle through a ford in the river. The unruly creatures splash water, to the displeasure of a peasant woman, who is also wading through the water. Another woman is mounted on a laden ox. Berchem combined the southern character of the landscape with the kind of pine trees that one would expect to see in the north.

artworks.title: Carriages and Waiting Coachmen
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 10.5 cm × height 31.5 cm x width 43 cm
artworks.description: It is a rainy day on the Malieveld, a large green in The Hague. The coachmen of the carriages for hire wait for passengers near the guardhouse. Coachmen generally wore colourful outfits, which in Amsterdam earned them the nickname ‘little monkeys’. Here, the bright colours are concealed under their rain capes. De Zwart, like Breitner, painted images of modern city life, but tended to favour tranquil street scenes.

artworks.title: The Descent from the Cross

artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 11 cm × height 232 cm x width 193 cm
artworks.description: Pieter Fransz. de Grebber (c. 1600 - c. 1653).The Descent from the Cross, 1633. The Haarlem-born Catholic painter Pieter de Grebber made this altarpiece in 1633 for the Church of St Gommarus and St Pancras in the Breedstraat in Enkhuizen. Pieter de Grebber was related by marriage to Augustinus de Wolff - pastor of the parish and the man who commissioned the work: De Wolff's brother was married to the artist's sister Maria Fransdr. de Grebber, who was herself a painter. She had painted a portrait of her brother-in-law in 1631. The painting is shown here in its original frame. The work is not in the best of conditions - the varnish has yellowed and become opaque. Purchased from H.J. Dierenbach, pastor of the Old Catholic Church in Enkhuizen, 1907.

artworks.title: Memorial Panel with Eight Male Portraits, probably Willem Jelysz van Soutelande and Family, with Saint James the Greater and the Van Soutelande Family Crest, inner left wing of an altarpiece

artworks.dimensions: support: height 101 cm x width 35.5 cm
artworks.description: Zijluik van een memoriestuk met acht portretten van mannen en negen van vrouwen, respectievelijk vergezeld van de heiligen Jacobus Major en Maria Magdalena. Op het linkerpaneel de knielende stichter Willem Jelysz van Soutelande (overl. 1515-16) in de wapenrusting van een ridder van de Broederschap van de Heilige Land. Voor zich een altaar met een opengeslagen boek, achter zich zeven mannen (zijn zoons?) en de heilige Jacobus Major. In de lucht een engel met het wapen van Jacob de Wael van Rozenburg (overl. 1524) een burger van Haarlem. Op het rechterpaneel (SK-A-1188-B) de knielende stichteres Kathrijn van der Graft Willemsdochter (overl. 1490-91), eveneens knielend in aanbidding voor een altaar met opengeslagen boek. Achter haar acht vrouwen (haar dochters?) en de heilige Maria Magdalena. In de lucht een engel met het wapen van Margriet van Waveren. Op de buitenzijden van de panelen staan de wapens van Van Soutelande en het alliantiewapen Van der Graft-Van Soutelande.

artworks.title: Pan Punished by Nymphs
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 76.8 cm x width 120 cm
artworks.description: Jacob Jordaens (1593 - 1678). Pan punished by the nymphs, c. 1640. In this playful mythological scene Pan, the goat-hoofed Greek god of the woods, is punished by the nymphs because, despite their attempts to teach him, he is still unable to dance. They have tied his hands behind his back and are cutting off his beard. Standing above the others is Apollo. As god of the arts, he directed the punishment. The subject is borrowed from the Eikones by Philostratus, a series of descriptions of fictional ancient paintings. Many artists had drawn inspiration from these narratives since the Renaissance. From the W.Six collection (Amsterdam) and G. Bicker van Swieten (The Hague). Purchased in 1809, as part of the collection Van Heteren Gevers. On loan to the Mauritshuis, The Hague, between 1948 and 2001.

artworks.artist: workshop of Michiel Jansz van Mierevelt
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: outer size: depth 5.8 cm (support incl. frame) × support: height 71.3 cm x width 58.8 cm
artworks.description: Maarten Harpertsz Tromp. Studio of M.J. van Miereveld, after an original of 1640. Admiral Maarten Harpertsz Tromp (1598-1653) was born into a seafaring family. In 1607, at the age of nine, he was on board his father's ship at the Battle of Gibraltar, fighting the Spanish fleet. He was to rise to the highest rank in the navy. In 1639 he inflicted a crucial defeat on Spain at the Battle of the Downs off the southeast coast of England. In 1652 Tromp was given command of the Dutch navy. That year, four years after peace had been signed with Spain, tension with England eventually led to war. Tromp was killed in 1653 in the Battle of Ter Heijde off the coast of South Holland which was won by the English.

artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. A remarkable aspect is the number of foreigners who fought for the Dutch. The Republic's army enjoyed an international reputation and attracted young noblemen from abroad. For them, the war was a career opportunity.

artworks.title: Portrait of Ernst Casimir (1573-1632), Count of Nassau-Dietz
artworks.artist: workshop of Michiel Jansz van Mierevelt
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 29.8 cm x width 24.2 cm
artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. A remarkable aspect is the number of foreigners who fought for the Dutch. The Republic's army enjoyed an international reputation and attracted young noblemen from abroad. For them, the war was a career opportunity.

artworks.title: Landscape with Rocky Cliffs and a Waterfall
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 61 cm x width 73 cm × height 78.5 cm x width 91.5 cm x thickness 8.5 cm
artworks.description: At the time of the Hague School, the French painter Courbet enjoyed a certain notoriety. He styled himself as a rebel and refused to align himself with any spe-cific style. Instead he began a one-man movement: ‘Realism’. He tried to render the ruggedness of nature by applying the paint to the canvas spontaneously, often with a palette knife. He painted these cliffs in the Jura Mountains in the vicinity of his native Ornans.

artworks.description: This sitter was a member of a prominent Dutch family. He served as bailiff and burgomaster of Alkmaar. In his right hand he holds a prayer nut encased in silver or gold, an extremely costly object for private devotion. He used it to demonstrate his piety, but also, and primarily, his affluence.

artworks.title: Virgin and Child

artworks.description: Towards the end of his career Lucas painted a few pictures of the Virgin and Child, including this one. The placement of the mother and child close to the picture plane lends the scene intimacy, which is further heightened by her tender caress. To create a personal bond with the viewer, Mary and Jesus gaze at us with striking directness.

artworks.title: Sultan Ahmed III

artworks.dimensions: height 33.5 cm x width 27 cm × weight 1.2 kg
artworks.description: Turkish culture blossomed under the rule of Ahmed III. The sultan was fascinated by tulips and organized lavish festivities that lasted as long as the flowers were in bloom. This period, known as the Tulip Era, witnessed many celebrations and was more openly receptive to Western influences. Vanmour saw Ahmed III on various occasions and so was able to give an accurate portrayal of his features.

artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, copper (metal), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 6 cm × support: height 40.3 cm x width 49.2 cm
artworks.description: Roelant Saverij (1578 - 1639). Elijah fed by the ravens, 1634. This woodland scene inhabited by animals depicts a story from the Old Testament. Elijah withdrew from the world and lived the life of a hermit, surviving on bread brought to him by ravens. At centre right we see Elijah; the ravens are more difficult to distinguish. Roelant Saverij came from Flanders, the cradle of landscape art. He was a court painter in Prague and from 1618 on was active in Utrecht. Painted on copper. Purchased in 1885.

artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 6 cm × height 52 cm x width 66 cm
artworks.description: Inauguration of the University of Ghent by the Prince of Orange in the throne room of the town hall, 9 October 181, by M.I. van Bree. Education played a major role in William I's attempt to promote national unity - from nursery school to university. The North had three universities (Leiden, Utrecht and Groningen). Since the French occupation the South no longer had any. Three universities were therefore established by Royal Decree: at Louvain, Liège and Ghent. The crown prince (the future King William II) is seated to the left of an empty throne above which is a portrait of King William I. He is listening to a speech by the commissioner general of Public Education, Science and Art. At his side are the vice chancellor, the mayor of Ghent and the president of the board of curators.

artworks.title: Two Ladies Examining a Little Painting
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 14 cm x width 11.5 cm × depth 8.3 cm
artworks.description: This meticulously painted scene of old maids in a humorous situation is typical of Bakker Korff. The viewer’s imagination is pricked. Are the two women actually examining a work of art, or are they coming to the realization while looking at their reflection in a mirror that they are no longer as pretty as a picture? Given the stuffy interior in which the ladies sit, the latter seems more likely.

artworks.description: Mooi Aal of 'De keuze tussen jong en oud'. Een eenvoudige jonge vrouw wendt zich af van een rijke oude man en een elegante jonge man en kiest voor een jongen die spottend naar zijn mededingers wijst. De oude man draagt een bontmuts en zit aan een tafel geldstukken te tellen, hij houdt een geldzak geopend. De jongeman heft een wijnglas in zijn linkerhand. artworks.title: Willem Joseph Baron van Gendt (1625-1672). Vice Admiral
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)

Two years later - in 1667 - Van Gendt commanded the first squadron to reach the English naval base at Chatham. He was killed fighting the English in the Battle of Sole Bay off the southeast coast of England.

artworks.description: Drieluik met de bewening. Op het middenpaneel de bewening van Christus in een landschap. Het lichaam van Christus ligt tegen de knie van Maria. Om haar heen de heilige vrouwen, Johannes, Jozef en een monnik. De bewening is een vrije kopie naar het schilderij van Geertgen tot Sint Jans in Wenen. Op de binnenzijde van het linker zijpaneel een knielende stichter met de heilige Petrus. Op de binnenzijde van het rechter zijpaneel de knielende stichteres met de heilige Paulus. Op de buitenzijde van de zijpanelen de wapens van stichter (de familie Speyart van Woerden) en zijn vrouw.

artworks.title: Portrait of Antonio van Diemen, Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 33 cm x width 25 cm × depth 3.8 cm
artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

Pieter Both, 1610-1614
Gerard Reynst, 1614-1615
Laurens Reael,1615-1619
Jan Pietersz Coen, 1619-1623 and 1627-1629
Pieter de Carpentier, 1623-1627
Jacques Specx, 1629-1632
Hendrick Brouwer, 1632-1636
Antonio van Diemen, 1636-1645
Cornelis van der Lijn, 1645-1650
Karel Reiniersz, 1650-1653
Joan Maetsuycker, 1653-1678
Rycklof van Goens, 1678-1681
Cornelis Speelman, 1681-1684
Johannes Camphuys, 1684-1691
Willem van Outshoorn, 1691-1704
Abraham van Riebeeck, 1709-1713
Christoffel van Swoll, 1713-1718
Hendrick Zwaardecroon, 1718-1725
Mattheus de Haan, 1725-1729

The portrait of Joan van Hoorn, 1704-1709, is missing.

The artist followed established conventions for depicting grief and sorrow through gesture. This approach was characteristic of the stiff, rather formulaic style derived from Greek and Byzantine models that was prevalent in 13th-century Italy.

artworks.title: Allegory of the Revival of the Dutch Herring Fishery after the Second Anglo-Dutch War (1665-67)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)

artworks.description: Allegory of the prosperity of the fishing industry, attributed to Willem Eversdijck, shortly after 1667. Michiel de Ruyter and other prominent admirals are hauling in a herring net and enjoying the fish. After the Republic's successes of the Second Anglo-Dutch War (1665-1667), the herring fishery was able to flourish again. Here the artist shows the importance of the protection of the Dutch navy for trade and fishing.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint), paper

artworks.description: Various European trade organizations had branches in the port of Canton. Because there was so much construction, the paintings can be easily dated. This is the situation in 1773. The ships are moored in the estuary of the Pearl River (Whampoa); the merchants’ offices were located upriver. During the off-season the European traders stayed in Macao, which was also in the mouth of the Pearl River.

Rechts de andere koningen met hun geschenken en gevolg. Op het linker zijpaneel de geknielde mannelijke schenker met zes zonen en de heilige Joris met een vaandel. Op de lessenaar het wapen van de familie Van Rooy. Op de rechter zijpaneel de geknielde vrouwelijk schenker met vijf dochters en de heilige Anna-te drieën. Hier het wapen van de familie Francken (of Vrancken).

artworks.description: Een aanrijding bij de Hallepoort te Brussel. Een vechtpartij tussen twee voerlieden na een botsing tussen twee wagens. Een vrouw spartelt tussen de omgevallen manden met groenten en melkbussen. Links het belastingkantoor en een fontein.

artworks.title: Portrait of A.M.L. Bonger-van der Linden
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 4.2 cm × height 72.5 cm x width 59.5 cm x thickness 3.3 cm
artworks.description: In 1888, Anne Marie Louise married Andries Bonger, a friend of Theo van Gogh (Vincent’s brother) and of the French painters Emile Bernard and Redon. Andries collected the work of these avant-garde artists, including self-portraits of Van Gogh and Bernard, on view elsewhere in this gallery. Using just two shades of paint, Redon succeeded in infusing this portrait with an air of delicate frailty.

artworks.title: Last Judgment and the Burying of the Dead

artworks.description: Het Laatste Oordeel en het begraven der doden, het zevende werk der Barmhartigheden. In het midden boven zit Christus op de wereldbol op de regenboog met opgeheven armen, de hemel is vol met engelen die op bazuinen blazen, het kruis met bijbel hooghouden en een zwaard of lelietak dragen. Op aarde verrijzen links de doden die gered worden, rechts de verdoemde zielen en duivels. In het midden begraven enkele mannen in het zwart een doodskist.

artworks.title: The Dutch Herring Fleet at the fishing grounds
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, biological material, materials by function, panel, ink
artworks.dimensions: height 84 cm x width 114 cm × depth 6.5 cm
artworks.description: The Dutch herringfleet by Pieter Vogelaer, second half 17th century. Herring was a vital Dutch export product, one of the mainstays of the republic's economy. Herring was a Dutch speciality of the fisherman of the Dutch towns along the river Maas and the Zuiderzee. With their large boats, they dominated herring fishing completely. The fish was cleaned at sea and then processed on shore.

artworks.title: Travellers among Roman Ruins with Rebecca and Eliezer at the Well
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, copper (metal), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 42 cm x width 58 cm × outer size: depth 6.5 cm (support incl. frame)
artworks.description: Willem van Nieulandt (1584 - 1636). Landscape with Roman ruins, c. 1605. In this landscape with ancient ruins we see a number of figures. The group of camels on the left suggests that they are biblical characters. Those near the fountain may represent the Old Testament figure of Rebecca, with Abraham's servant. The ruins in the painting are authentic - they stood in the Forum Romanum in Rome - but here the painter has arbitrarily located them in the midst of an imaginary landscape. Painted on copper. Purchased in 1809 (as the work of Paulus Bril), as part of the Van Heteren Gevers collection (The Hague).

artworks.title: Portrait of Louis Royer

artworks.description: The couple Louis Royer and Carolina Kerst were captured in a portrait after their return from a yearlong sojourn in Rome. Louis is seen in his sculptor’s studio surrounded by his work, some of which is on view in this gallery. One of his sculptures is visible in Carolina’s likeness. A letter and an Italian landscape allude to their Italian trip and the cross around her neck signifies her Catholic faith.

Zoutman is portrayed with the decorations he received in gratitude from Stadtholder William V: a gold sword, a Dogger Bank medallion on a ribbon and a medal of honour.

Links neemt de zoon afscheid van zijn vader, daarachter drinkt hij met een vrouw aan een tafel buiten een herberg. artworks.title: Landscape with the baptism of the eunuch
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 7.1 cm × height 98.1 cm x width 130.2 cm x thickness 3.7 cm
artworks.description: Herman van Swanevelt (c. 1600 - 1655). Landscape with the baptism of the eunuch, c. 1635. Herman van Swanevelt lived for many years in Rome, where he did this painting. He is known for his sunny, wooded landscapes with hazy panoramas that form the backdrop for a story. Here the subject is the biblical account of the baptism of the eunuch, a popular theme in the 17th century. The apostle Philip met an African eunuch on one of his journeys and converted him. The man then asked to be baptised. Purchased in 1979.

artworks.title: The Princess of Orange Receiving Alexander II (1818-1881), Grand Duke and Heir to the Throne of Russia, in the Czar Peter's House in Zaandam, 17 April 1839
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 118.5 cm x width 144.5 cm x thickness 3.2 cm × depth 11 cm
artworks.description: Anna Paulowna, de prinses van Oranje, ontvangt Alexander II, grootvorst en troonopvolger van Rusland, in het Czaar Peterhuisje te Zaandam, 17 april 1839. De prinses presenteert de grootvorst een blad waarop brood (in tulbandvorm) en zout in een zoutvat, een bekend Russisch welkomstritueel. Aanwezig zijn (van links naar rechts): prins Willem Alexander Frederik (Alexander) van Oranje-Nassau, prins Willem Frederik Hendrik (Hendrik) van Oranje-Nassau, Elisa Martha, gravin van Limburg Stirum, Sophia Wilhelmina Petronella, gravin van Wassenaar, prins Willem (III) van Oranje-Nassau, Dieuwke Fontein, haar echtgenoot Adriaan van der Hoop, prins Willem Frederik Karel (Frederik) der Nederlanden, prinses Anna Paulowna van Rusland, prinses Louisa van Pruisen, prins Willem II van Oranje-Nassau, Alexander II van Rusland, zijn aide-de-camp Graaf Orloff en tussen de figuren bij de deur Baron d'Ivoy en Baron Mackay.

artworks.dimensions: height 75 cm x width 62.6 cm
artworks.description:
The most prominent cardinal in Rome ordered this painting as a gift for a French minister and his wife, whose name, Catherine Félicité, inspired the choice of subject. The Christian martyr Saint Felicity – here in a yellow gown – was forced to witness the martyrdom of her seven sons before herself being beheaded. Trevisani included two self-portraits: as the standing man at left, and as the man looking out at us from
behind the statue at right.

artworks.title: Portrait of Lodewijk (1538-74), Count of Nassau
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 29.6 cm x width 24 cm x thickness 0.7 cm × outer size: depth 3.2 cm (support incl. frame)
artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. A remarkable aspect is the number of foreigners who fought for the Dutch. The Republic's army enjoyed an international reputation and attracted young noblemen from abroad. For them, the war was a career opportunity.

artworks.description: The subjects for this painting and its pendant (right of the mantelpiece) come from the Metamorphoses, famous stories by the Roman author Ovid. In the other painting, he passes himself off as Diana, goddess of the hunt, in order to charm her nymph Callisto.

artworks.artist: attributed to Aert van den Bossche
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 97.3 cm x width 68.5 cm × sight size: height 97 cm x width 68 cm × frame: height 118 cm x width 89.5
artworks.description: A lamb and a goat are sacrificed to a golden idol in a temple in the heart of a Late Gothic town. The kneeling priest might be St Augustine, the Church Father who in his youth had embraced Manichaeism. However, after converting to Christianity, he fervently refuted this once widespread early religion. Made in Brussels, the panel probably was part of an altarpiece or series of paintings featuring scenes from Augustine’s life.

artworks.title: Johan Melchior Kemper (1776-1824), Jurist and Statesman
artworks.artist: David Pièrre Giottino Humbert de Superville
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 38 cm x width 28.9 cm x thickness 1 cm × depth 7.3 cm
artworks.description: Joan Melchior Kemper (1776 - 1824) by D.P.G. Humbert de Superville, c. 1815. Former Patriot Kemper was the author of the proclamation with which Prince William of Orange presented himself as 'William I, sovereign lord' on 2 December 1813, a few days after arriving in the Netherlands. In it William I promised a constitution guaranteeing the freedom of his subjects. As a professor the jurist Kemper was the mentor of many later politicians such as Thorbecke and Groen van Prinsterer. In 1817 Kemper became a member of the Lower House. Kemper's decorations are the symbols of Commander of the Orde van de Nederlandse Leeuw. The order was established in 1815. Kemper was a personal friend of the painter. Humbert gave Kemper's daughters drawing lessons. And Kemper had ensured that Humbert was appointed lecturer at Leiden University in 1814.

artworks.description: Jacob Baron van Wassenaer, Lord of Obdam, by Abraham Westervelt, c. 1673. Born into an old Dutch noble family (1610-1665) Obdam began his career in the Republic's territorial army. This offered better prospects for aristocrats than the navy. Nevertheless, in1653 Obdam transferred to the fleet. He became lieutenant admiral on the death of Maarten Tromp. Obdam was killed at the start of the Second Anglo-Dutch War (1665-1667) in the Battle of Lowestoft off England's east coast.

On 7 October 1782 the Republic and the United States signed a treaty of trade and friendship in The Hague. Two personifications: the Netherlands, on the right with a liberty hat on a spear, offers a hand to America. Meanwhile, an Indian holds a horn of plenty. The fruit from the cornucopia and the tobacco roll in the foreground on the left refer to the results that the treaty was expected to produce.

artworks.title: The Burial of Father Joannes Vitus Janssen (1803-43) at Paramaribo
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 53.5 cm x width 70 cm × depth 5.7 cm
artworks.description: Funeral in Paramaribo of the missionary Joannes Vitus Janssen, 1843. Anonymous, c. 1843. The coffin is borne by twelve black pall bearers dressed in white to symbolise mourning. Two priests walk behind the coffin: Petrus Donders, known as the 'apostle of the Indians and lepers of Surinam', and T. Kempkes. They are followed by the church councillors, the governor's staff and various officers. Around 1,400 black Surinamers, all Catholic converts, attended the funeral. In the foreground, left, is an Indian family. Preceding the coffin are the funeral directors, members of the Kreps family. Their surname became a byword for a gravedigger in Surinam.The Catholic cemetery was opened in 1840. Slaves were buried in a separate section, probably at the back, to the left.

artworks.title: Portrait of Justinus of Nassau (1559-1631)
artworks.artist: workshop of Jan Antonisz van Ravesteyn
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 29.4 cm x width 24.1 cm x thickness 1 cm
artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. A remarkable aspect is the number of foreigners who fought for the Dutch. The Republic's army enjoyed an international reputation and attracted young noblemen from abroad. For them, the war was a career opportunity.

artworks.title: Perseus and Andromeda. Allegory of the liberation of the Netherlands by Prince Frederik Hendrik
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 29.2 cm x width 38.8 cm × depth 5.5 cm
artworks.description:
Koningin Henrietta Maria, vrouw van Karel I van Engeland bezocht de Republiek in 1642-1643. Aanleiding was de aflevering van haar dochtertje Mary Stuart die kort tevoren als 10-jarig meisje was getrouwd met de 15-jarige prins Willem II. Tegelijkertijd echter trachtte zij geldelijke steun te verkrijgen op onderpand van de kroonjuwelen voor de Engelse strijd die de koning tegen het Engelse parlement voerde.
Frederik Hendrik steunde de koning; de Staten-Generaal het parlement.
De hier afgebeelde scene was ontworpen als één der tableaux vivants bij de ontvangst van de koningin in Amsterdam. Hier wordt Frederik Hendrik (Perseus) belaagd door de vuurspuwende Spaanse tirannie, waarvan hij de Nederlanden (Andromeda) wist te bevrijden.
Dit tafereel zou geplaatst worden in het Damrak. Omdat de koningin over land de stad binnenkwam, werd het nooit uitgevoerd.

artworks.description: The Battle of Bautersem, by C. Kruseman, 1839. The Dutch and Belgian armies clashed on 12 August 1831 near Louvain. Commanded by the crown prince, the future King William II, the Dutch army won the day. This was the last action in the Ten Day Battle. The painting shows a moment of heroism: the prince exchanges his wounded horse in order to join the fight again undaunted. This sketch was for a large canvas at the Royal Palace in Amsterdam. artworks.title: Ladies’ Outing at Hünkâr İskelesi along the Bosporus

artworks.description: In summer, wealthy inhabitants of Istanbul fled the hot and humid city in search of cooler weather along the banks of the Bosporus. These outings were virtually the only diversion that women could enjoy outside their homes. The women of the sultan’s harem sometimes went on picnics. Vanmour probably painted one such occasion here. A black eunuch stands guard to keep out uninvited guests (men).

artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. A remarkable aspect is the number of foreigners who fought for the Dutch. The Republic's army enjoyed an international reputation and attracted young noblemen from abroad. For them, the war was a career opportunity.

artworks.description:
Wouwerman is known for his paintings of army camps, cavalry battles and hunting scenes, in which deftly
painted horses always play an important role. Thanks to his eye for detail, these paintings are very lively and anecdotal. In this painting, too, emphasis lies on narrative detail: some horses are being saddled, while a woman and child just manage to avoid being kicked by one of the animals.

artworks.title: Portrait of Inspector-General A.F. Goudriaan
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 9.7 cm × height 95.4 cm x width 79.5 cm x thickness 3.6 cm
artworks.description: Adriaan François Goudriaan, by Izaak Schouman, 1829. After 1800 the water authority administration was radically centralised. In 1808 it was decided to divide the country into two water-authority districts. Adriaan François Goudriaan (1768-1829) was appointed inspector general of the northeast district. It was his initiative to introduce the 'Amsterdamsch Peil': a standard water level for the whole country. Goudriaan is portrayed in his official uniform. He is wearing two insignias. One was received from the French emperor Napoleon, the other from King William I. Goudriaan served both rulers as a civil servant: the various changes of regime in the years after 1800 did not damage his career.

artworks.description:
Anthony de Wale (Walaeus), 1573-1639, contra-remonstrants theoloog. Door David Bailly. Gedateerd 1636.
De Wale studeerde in Leiden bij Gomarus, de voorman van de latere contra-remonstranten. Hij was predikant en leraar in Middelburg en vanaf 1619 hoogleraar in Leiden. Walaeus nam actief deel aan de Synode van Dordrecht en werd daar door Maurits naar Den Haag ontboden om Van Oldenbarnevelt in zijn laatste ogenblikken bij te staan.

artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: thickness 4 cm × height 16.9 cm x width 13.7 cm x depth 0.6 cm
artworks.description: Willem Usselincx. Anonymous, 1637. After the Sack of Antwerp by Spanish troops, the merchant Willem Usselincx (1567-1647) settled in Middelburg. He fervently supported the foundation of a West India Company as an instrument in the war against Spain. But as a truce with the Spaniards drew nearer, his plans were rejected. Yet the declared objectives of the West India Company that was established directly after the Twelve Year Truce ended in 1621, were not what Usselincx had wanted: there was not enough emphasis on founding colonies and sending missionaries. Nevertheless, Usselincx is generally seen as the spiritual father of the WIC, as this portrait proclaims: 'Author of the West India Company'.

artworks.title: Portrait of Johan Ernst I (1582-1617), Count of Nassau-Siegen
artworks.artist: workshop of Jan Antonisz van Ravesteyn
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 29.7 cm x width 24.1 cm x thickness 1 cm
artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. A remarkable aspect is the number of foreigners who fought for the Dutch. The Republic's army enjoyed an international reputation and attracted young noblemen from abroad. For them, the war was a career opportunity.

artworks.description: In 1834, when J.C. Baud was the governor-general, an earthquake struck Buitenzorg (Bogor) Palace. Upon his return to the Netherlands Baud engaged Willem Troost to paint two pictures of his former residence: one before and one after the earthquake. Troost had never been to Indonesia and must have relied on sketches made by other artists. The injured woman on the chairs in the left foreground is probably Baud’s wife.

artworks.title: Portrait of Justus de Huybert, Clerk of the States of Zeeland and of the Admiralty

artworks.dimensions: height 53 cm x width 44 cm × depth 5.2 cm
artworks.description: Justus de Huybert. Zeeland school, c. 1665. Justus de Huybert (1610-1682) was secretary of the States of Zeeland. The same function he held with the Zeeland Admiralty. Like many prominent contemporaries, Huybert had his portrait painted wearing a Japanese gown, and on his head a skullcap. In the background: the assembly hall of the States of Zeeland in the Abbey of Middelburg.

artworks.title: Portrait of Jan Heemskerk Azn (1818-1897)

artworks.title: Portrait of Dirck, Johannes, or Jacobus Wallis
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: outer size: depth 5.5 cm (support incl. SK-L-6065) × support: height 85.1 cm x width 65.7 cm x thickness 1.3 cm
artworks.description: Along with Frans Hals, Cornelis Verspronck was the most sought-after portraitist in Haarlem. Burghers who deemed Hals’ brushstrokes to be too loose, turned to him. Verspronck’s realistic portrait style is brilliantly exemplified in this likeness of a member of the Wallis family, which is laid out in detail in a sober and serene manner. Quite exceptionally it is still in its original frame. A rarity!

artworks.title: Three Peaches on a Stone Plinth
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, paper, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 28.7 cm x width 21.2 cm × height 35.2 cm x width 29 cm x thickness 2.7 cm
artworks.description: Coorte portrayed with the precision of a scientist. By isolating it, it is as if he wanted to get to the very essence of a peach or a gooseberry. Although these four paintings were not conceived as a series, they have formed an ensemble since the second half of the 18th century.

artworks.title: Wedding procession on the Bosphorus
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 56 cm x width 90 cm × weight 5.6 kg
artworks.description: A colourful procession along the Bosporus leads a bride to the house of her future husband. She is mounted on horseback under a baldachin carried by four men. Walking directly in front of the tent is the imam, the religious leader, who will consecrate their marriage. The pyramidal tower made of gold thread in the shape of ears of corn is a symbol of fertility.

artworks.title: Portrait of a Woman, probably Morosina Morosini, Wife of Marino Grimani, the Doge of Venice
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 114 cm x width 97.5 cm × depth 10 cm
artworks.description: Portret van een vrouw, waarschijnlijk Morosina Morosini, de echtgenote van Marino Grimani, doge van Venetië (in 1595). Kniestuk, zittend in een stoel.

artworks.title: The Camp Follower
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 56.1 cm x width 70.9 cm x thickness 1.5 cm × depth 10 cm
artworks.description: De marketentster of zoetelaarster. Een groep soldaten verzameld bij de tent van een marketentster. Een vrouw schenkt een glas wijn in voor een soldaat die tegenover haar op zijn trommel zit. Naast haar een staande soldaat met een hoge muts  en een bijl in de rechterhand, een glas wijn in de linker. Links een minnekozend paar onder een afdekje. Rechts probeert een jongetje met een hond iets te verkopen. Rechts op de achtergrond meer figuren rond een open vuur.

artworks.title: Julius Civilis Having his Hair Cut after the Fall of Vetera, while his Son Kills Some of the Captives

artworks.description: In 1613, the Dutch parliament (States General) commissioned Otto van Veen to paint twelve paintings depicting the revolt of the Batavians against the Romans in AD 69 and 70. These were displayed in Binnenhof, the central government building in The Hague. In the early years of the Dutch Republic, many compared their own revolt against Spain to the Batavian uprising.

artworks.title: Cornelis Calkoen on his Way to his Audience with Sultan Ahmed III
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: weight 12.2 kg × height 91.5 cm x width 125 cm
artworks.description: Calkoen’s audience with Sultan Ahmed III took place on 14 September 1727 and followed a strict protocol. Here we see the retinue, unarmed according to convention, enter-ing the second courtyard of Topkapı Palace. Audiences were always held on the day that the Janissaries, the elite fighting force, received their pay. Just as Calkoen enters, the soldiers lunge noisily at the dishes of rice.

Geschilderd op een koperen plaat, oorspronkelijk gebruikt als drukplaat voor textiel. Onderdeel van een reeks van portretten van de gouverneurs-generaal van het voormalige Nederlands Oost-Indië.

artworks.description: Bij de kinderwagen op het strand. Een vrouw buigt zich over het kind in een kinderwagen. Op de voorgrond een zittende vrouw met een rammelaar in de hand, links een koffer. Rechtsboven een doorkijkje naar het strand.

artworks.title: Moses Choosing the seventy Elders

artworks.description: Mozes verkiest de zeventig oudsten. In een vlakte in de woestijn staat Mozes met uitgestrekte armen tussen de Israëlieten. Op de achtergrond het tabernakel of ark des verbonds, rechts palmbomen en tenten. Modello voor het grote schilderij in de vroedschapskamer van het voormalige Stadhuis op de Dam.

artworks.title: Virgin and Child
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, biological material, panel
artworks.dimensions: height 145 cm x width 76 cm x depth 12 cm × height 111 cm x width 54 cm
artworks.description: Maria zittend op een bank met het Christuskind op schoot. Met geïntegreerde lijst.

artworks.title: Three Views of the Pearl River: Canton, Macao, Whampoa
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint), paper
artworks.dimensions: height 52 cm x width 76 cm
artworks.description: Various European trade organizations had branches in the port of Canton. Because there was so much construction, the paintings can be easily dated. This is the situation in 1773. The ships are moored in the estuary of the Pearl River (Whampoa); the merchants’ offices were located upriver. During the off-season the European traders stayed in Macao, which was also in the mouth of the Pearl River.

artworks.title: The Raising of Lazarus
artworks.artist: attributed to Aertgen Claesz van Leyden
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 75.7 cm x width 78.8 cm
artworks.description: This triptych was painted to commemorate a married couple, the man and woman shown kneeling on the wings. The central panel appropriately depicts the miracle of Christ raising Lazarus from the dead, an allusion to the promise of eternal life and the belief that death is overcome through faith in Christ.

artworks.description: Portret van Jacobus Scheltema, geschiedschrijver. Buste, en face. Kopie door Idsinga naar het origineel door Van der Kooi.

artworks.title: Portrait of the Engraver Jan Caspar Philips

artworks.description: Familieportret van Willem Philip Kops, koopman te Haarlem, met zijn vrouw Johanna de Vos en kinderen. De kinderen zijn Willem Kops, Catharina Kops (met een hondje op de arm), Jacobus de Vos Kops, Philip Kops en François Kops. Twee van de jongens hebben een bok bij zich.

artworks.description: The office of reis effendi or reisü’l küttab, the head of the chancery, could be likened to the minister of foreign affairs. This official at the Ottoman court had the most contact with Western diplomats. Ambassador Calkoen would have met him on a regular basis.

artworks.title: View of Heusden

artworks.description: Gezicht op de stad Heusden van de overzijde van de rivier, op het water varen allerlei scheepjes.

artworks.title: Landscape with a Hunter and other Figures
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 67 cm x width 63 cm × depth 12.5 cm
artworks.description: Jan Wijnants (1631/32 - 1684). Landscape with a hunter and other figures, c. 1670. A half-dead tree dominates this work, a motif which the artist borrowed from Jacob van Ruisdael. Jan Wijnants produced a great many paintings, not all of them of equally high quality. From 1660 on he lived in Amsterdam, where Philips Wouwerman was one of the most sought-after landscape artists of his day. Jan Wijnants undoubtedly studied the work of his successful fellow Amsterdammer. Bequest of A. van der Hoop, 1854. On loan from the city of Amsterdam, 1885.

artworks.title: Willem Crul (1721-81), Rear Admiral
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 9.3 cm × height 113 cm x width 88 cm
artworks.description: De Vierde Engelse Oorlog (1780-1784) verliep desastreus voor de Republiek. De Nederlandse oorlogsvloot was geen partij voor de Engelsen. Economische malaise en politieke crisis waren het gevolg van deze oorlog. Velen wilden de werkelijkheid niet onder ogen zien. De onbesliste zeeslag bij Doggersbank (1781) werd in de Republiek gevierd als een overwinning. Bij de in 1784 in Parijs gesloten vrede moest de VOC haar prominente positie in Azië prijsgeven.

Behoort samen met SK-A-2359 tot een reeks van passievoorstellingen waarvan de andere delen zich bevinden in Aschaffenburg.

artworks.title: The Archangel Gabriel Appearing to Zacharias

artworks.title: Adriaan Valckenier (1737-1741)
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, brass (alloy), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 102.5 cm x width 85.5 cm
artworks.description: The highest-ranking Dutch East India Company (VOC) official in Asia was the governor-general. He presided in the Castle of Batavia (now Jakarta, Indonesia), a fort built by the Dutch. The assembly hall in the Castle of Batavia was the centre of Dutch power in Asia. The walls were hung with portraits of all of the governors-general. Most of the 18th-century examples shown here were painted in Asia, often by anony¬mous artists.

artworks.title: Portrait of Jacomina Claesdr van Ruyven (died 1509), Wife of Arent Franckensz van der Meer

artworks.title: A Bleaching Field
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 41 cm x width 57 cm × depth 12 cm
artworks.description: Women are busy doing laundry near a French village church. One of them spreads the linen on the bleaching field, while another fetches water from the pump. Maris divided the space into three areas by placing a fence between the women and an autumnal-brown hedge before the church. The saplings’ delicate branches reinforce the horizontal lines of the composition.

artworks.title: Juno Commanding Argus to Keep Watch on Io

artworks.dimensions: depth 8.1 cm × height 24.5 cm x width 31.5 cm
artworks.description: Juno geeft de herder Argus opdracht Io te bewaken. Links Io in de gedaante van een koe. Achter Juno haar triomfwagen en twee pauwen.

artworks.title: Muleteers at an Inn
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, copper (metal), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 34 cm x width 43.5 cm
artworks.description: With a few carefully chosen motifs, Dujardin is able to transport us to Italy – to the courtyard of an inn, where muleteers with their laden beasts have stopped to rest. It is warm and the locals have sought shade to escape the heat. Even the little donkey stands in the shadow cast by the larger animals. Above the door hang two empty fiaschi, large wine bottles covered with raffia. All of this conjures up memories of the south.

artworks.title: Italian Landscape with Shepherds and Animals at a Fountain

artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, copper (metal), oil paint (paint)

artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

artworks.title: Jacob Cornelisz Banjaert, called van Neck (1564-1638), Admiral, Burgomaster and Councilor of Amsterdam
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 102 cm x width 82 cm × depth 10.5 cm
artworks.description: Jacob Cornelisz van Neck, by Cornelis Ketel, 1605. Amsterdam's Jacob van Neck (1564-1638) was merchant, discoverer and public official, a combination far from rare in the early half of the 17th century. In 1598-1599 Van Neck commanded the first successful Dutch trading expedition to Asia. He sailed there again the next year. After his return, in 1603, Van Neck remained in Amsterdam. He turned from sailor to patrician, holding major posts in the administrations of both city and Republic. Van Neck's right hand is hidden from view. He had been wounded on his second voyage to Asia during an encounter with the Portuguese off the island of Tidore, and had lost some of his fingers.

Lingelbach made sketches from life in Rome, from which he composed this imaginary marketplace after he returned to Amsterdam. The figures take no interest in the antique ruins; their attention is absorbed by the
tooth-puller at the left, who treats his victim while on horseback. In the centre, two men play morra (which
involves them guessing how many fingers their opponent will hold up). At right is a ciambellaro selling
pretzels and other refreshments.

artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. artworks.title: Portrait of Cornelis Speelman, Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 33 cm x width 25 cm × depth 3.7 cm
artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

Pieter Both, 1610-1614
Gerard Reynst, 1614-1615
Laurens Reael,1615-1619
Jan Pietersz Coen, 1619-1623 and 1627-1629
Pieter de Carpentier, 1623-1627
Jacques Specx, 1629-1632
Hendrick Brouwer, 1632-1636
Antonio van Diemen, 1636-1645
Cornelis van der Lijn, 1645-1650
Karel Reiniersz, 1650-1653
Joan Maetsuycker, 1653-1678
Rycklof van Goens, 1678-1681
Cornelis Speelman, 1681-1684
Johannes Camphuys, 1684-1691
Willem van Outshoorn, 1691-1704
Abraham van Riebeeck, 1709-1713
Christoffel van Swoll, 1713-1718
Hendrick Zwaardecroon, 1718-1725
Mattheus de Haan, 1725-1729

The portrait of Joan van Hoorn, 1704-1709, is missing.

artworks.title: Portrait of William (1592-1642), Count of Nassau-Siegen
artworks.artist: workshop of Jan Antonisz van Ravesteyn
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: outer size: depth 2 cm (support incl. frame) × support: height 30.4 cm x width 24.3 cm x thickness 1.3 cm
artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. A remarkable aspect is the number of foreigners who fought for the Dutch. The Republic's army enjoyed an international reputation and attracted young noblemen from abroad. For them, the war was a career opportunity.

artworks.artist: workshop of Jan Antonisz van Ravesteyn
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: outer size: depth 0.5 cm (support incl. frame) × support: height 30.3 cm x width 24.7 cm x thickness 1 cm
artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. A remarkable aspect is the number of foreigners who fought for the Dutch. The Republic's army enjoyed an international reputation and attracted young noblemen from abroad. For them, the war was a career opportunity.

artworks.title: De beschieting van de Kraton van de Sultan van Djambi door de gouvernementsmarineschepen 'Celebes', 'Admiraal van Kinsbergen' en 'Onrust' op 8 september 1858
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 9 cm × height 70.5 cm x width 100 cm
artworks.description: The barrage of the Sultan of Djambi's kraton on Sumatra by three Dutch paddlesteamers, 5 September 1858. Following the refusal by the new sultan of Djambi, on eastern Sumatra, to recognise Dutch sovereignty in the East Indies, a military campaign was organised against him in 1858. The sultan's throne was declared forfeit and his kraton (palace) was captured. He fled inland. His successor agreed that in future Djambi would remain part of the Dutch East Indies and subject to colonial authority. The anonymous artist portrayed the paddlesteamers Celebes, Admiral van Kinsbergen and Onrust bombarding the kraton from Djambi river.

artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 33 cm x width 25 cm × depth 3.7 cm
artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

Pieter Both, 1610-1614
Gerard Reynst, 1614-1615
Laurens Reael,1615-1619

artworks.title: Isaac de l'Ostal de Saint-Martin (c 1629-96), Councillor of the Dutch East Indies and Commander of the Garrison at Batavia
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 132 cm x width 102 cm × depth 5 cm
artworks.description: Isaac de l'Ostal de Saint-Martin, by Jan de Baen (?) (c. 1660-1670). Frenchman Isaac de l'Ostal de Saint-Martin (c. 1629-1696) enjoyed a glorious career as a soldier in the service of the VOC between 1657 and 1683. He was stationed at Sri Lanka (Ceylon), Malabar and Ternate. He also fought several hostile Indonesians. In 1683 De Saint-Martin returned to the Netherlands in command of a fleet, only to return two years later to Batavia. He was appointed to the council of the Indies. Chaired by the governor-general, this body was the Dutch administration in Asia. De Saint-Martin remained on the council until his death in 1696. De Saint Martin is depicted as a senior military officer, rather than as a bureaucrat. In his hand is his staff of command. The painting must have been made in the Netherlands, perhaps during his short stay here, or perhaps even earlier.

artworks.description: Second police action at Yogyakarta, Mohammad Toha, 1949. Mohammad Toha was 11 when the Dutch army occupied his native Yogyakarta during the second police action. Toha pretended to be a cigarette vendor accompanied by his mother. In fact he kept his painting equipment in his cigarette box. He made sketches on scraps of paper and painted the final versions at home.

artworks.title: View of Tripoli
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 62.6 cm x width 109.4 cm x thickness 3.5 cm × depth 6 cm
artworks.description: Four views of North-African cities. Reinier Nooms, c. 1665. To protect the Dutch merchant fleet, the navy took the fight the enemy, far beyond the country's coastal waters. The Mediterranean harbours shown here - Algiers, Tunis, Tripoli and Salee - were bases from which privateers attacked Dutch merchant shipping. Attempts were made to impose treaties on these cities using the threat of naval force. Between 1661 and 1663 Admiral Michiel de Ruyter cruised the Mediterranean Sea in an effort to stamp out piracy. De Ruyter's ship, de Liefde, is shown in the foreground of the view of Algiers. This series of paintings was displayed in one of the rooms of the Amsterdam Admiralty. The Republic's navy was divided into five regional admiralties, one of which was based in Amsterdam.

artworks.title: Portrait of Albert (1596-1626), Count of Nassau-Dillenburg

artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. A remarkable aspect is the number of foreigners who fought for the Dutch. The Republic's army enjoyed an international reputation and attracted young noblemen from abroad. For them, the war was a career opportunity.

artworks.title: Portrait of Huybert Duyfhuys (c. 1515-81), Pastor of the Church of St James, Utrecht
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 5.8 cm × height 18.7 cm x width 11.9 cm
artworks.description:
Huibert Duyfhuis, ca. 1515-1581, pastoor van de Sint Laurenskerk te Rotterdam en van de Sint Jacobskerk te Utrecht. Na 1577 hervormd predikant te Utrecht. Copie uit 1669 naar een verloren origineel door H.M. Sorgh.
Duyfhuis, een typische overgangsfiguur, was in Rotterdam heimelijk gehuwd en had drie kinderen. In 1572 vluchtte hij voor de Spanjaarden naar Keulen. Na het overlijden van zijn vrouw werd hij in 1574 benoemd tot pastoor in Utrecht. Hier trachtte deze zeer tolerante prediker in zijn parochie eredienst en prediking in reformatorische zin te hervormen zonder de Calvinistische tucht te erkennen. De Utrechtse raad stond hem toe Gods woord te verbreiden 'soo 't behoort en soo hij dat voor Godt verantwoorden wil'. Willem van Oranje achtte Duyfhuis de ideale hervormde predikant. Het was kenmerkend dat hij de liturgische gewaden bleef dragen en de beelden in zijn kerk handhaafde.

artworks.title: The Standard Bearer

artworks.dimensions: height 102.6 cm x width 97.5 cm x depth 3.2 cm x height 118.8 cm x width 96.8 cm
artworks.description: Rembrandt’s ensign proudly poses near a column, the symbol of fortitude, his dagger within reach. Ensigns carried the banner of the civic guard or army. They had to defend this symbol with their life. When Rembrandt painted The Standard Bearer he had just begun working for himself and was experimenting with a loose painting style. Rembrandt took himself as the model: the face behind the walrus moustache is recognizably his own.

After a succession of posts in the VOC, Adam van Westerwolt (1580-1639) was appointed to the East Indies Council, an important position within the VOC in Asia. In 1637 he was sent as admiral of a VOC-fleet to blockade Portuguese trade in the Indian city of Goa. Van Westerwolt commissioned this portrait shortly before leaving for Asia. On the table is an astrolabe, a navigational instrument.

artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 33 cm x width 25 cm × depth 3.7 cm
artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

Pieter Both, 1610-1614
Gerard Reynst, 1614-1615
Laurens Reael,1615-1619
Jan Pietersz Coen, 1619-1623 and 1627-1629
Pieter de Carpentier, 1623-1627
Jacques Specx, 1629-1632
Hendrick Brouwer, 1632-1636
Antonio van Diemen, 1636-1645
Cornelis van der Lijn, 1645-1650
Karel Reiniersz, 1650-1653
Joan Maetsuycker, 1653-1678
Rycklof van Goens, 1678-1681
Cornelis Speelman, 1681-1684

artworks.description: The Birdwatchers and The Anglers, also on this wall, are both full of sexual allusions. While the mood in The Anglers is still cheerful and amorous, here the atmosphere is menacing. Birding is synonymous with making love; however, the consent does not seem to be mutual. One of the women is being assaulted, while the other two come to her aid. The bird the man forces on her was a well-known symbol for the male sex organ.

artworks.description: Tyrolean glass painters often used engravings by the Italian artist Marcantonio Raimondi as a model. artworks.title: Portrait of Pieter de Carpentier, Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 33 cm x width 25 cm × depth 3.7 cm
artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

Pieter Both, 1610-1614
Gerard Reynst, 1614-1615
Laurens Reael,1615-1619
Jan Pietersz Coen, 1619-1623 and 1627-1629
Pieter de Carpentier, 1623-1627
Jacques Specx, 1629-1632
Hendrick Brouwer, 1632-1636

Cornelis van der Lijn, 1645-1650

Joan Maetsuycker, 1653-1678

Cornelis Speelman, 1681-1684

artworks.artist: workshop of Jan Antonisz van Ravesteyn

artworks.dimensions: support: height 29.7 cm x width 24.1 cm x thickness 1.2 cm × outer size: depth 3.4 cm (support incl. frame)
artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. A remarkable aspect is the number of foreigners who fought for the Dutch. The Republic's army enjoyed an international reputation and attracted young noblemen from abroad. For them, the war was a career opportunity.

artworks.dimensions: height 101.5 cm x width 83.5 cm
artworks.description: The highest-ranking Dutch East India Company (VOC) official in Asia was the governor-general. He presided in the Castle of Batavia (now Jakarta, Indonesia), a fort built by the Dutch. The assembly hall in the Castle of Batavia was the centre of Dutch power in Asia. The walls were hung with portraits of all of the governors-general. Most of the 18th-century examples shown here were painted in Asia, often by anony¬mous artists.

artworks.description: The Collegium Medicum consisted of doctors and apothecaries and oversaw the practice of medicine in Amsterdam. The second man from the left, apothecary Jeronimo de Bosch, is known to have supplied the medicine chest to the slave ship Leusden, which ran aground off Suriname in 1738. This shipwreck became infamous because sailors locked the hatches of the lower deck. Consequently, 664 West-African men, women and children were trapped inside and perished.

artworks.description: Allegorie op de dood van J.D. van der Capellen door H.W. Schweickhardt, ca. 1785. De Overijsselse edelman Joan Derk van der Capellen (1741-1784) was de belangrijkste ideoloog van de patriotten. Door zijn vroege dood tijdens de hoogtijdagen van de patriottenbeweging werd hij voor zijn medestanders een held. De treurende vrouw, links van het borstbeeldvan Van der Capellen, stelt de vrijheid voor. De landarbeider rechts, het gebroken juk en de slavenketen verwijzen naar de afschaffingvan gedwongen arbeid van horige boeren voor hun landheer. Van der Capellen had zich voor die afschaffing ingezet.

artworks.title: Portrait of Jacques Specx, Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 6 cm × height 33 cm x width 25 cm
artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

Pieter Both, 1610-1614
Gerard Reynst, 1614-1615

artworks.description: Het groepsportret toont de borstbeelden van vier mannen met lang haar (pruiken) die zijn gehuld in antieke toga's. De man geheel rechts houdt een tekening vast waarop Chronos als personificatie van de tijd is afgebeeld die de vleugels van Cupido kortwiekt. Op de rechterachtergrond van de tekening, die met de letters G.F. is gesigneerd, is een pilaar met zandloper afgebeeld als teken van  vergankelijkheid. De tekening wordt mede vastgehouden door de tweede persoon van links, met de rode mantel, die in zijn andere hand een krijthouder vasthoudt. De geportretteerden zijn gesitueerd in een binnenruimte met links op de achtergrond een arcade met klassieke architectuur en met rechts een reliëf in medaillonvorm, waarop een jongen is te zien die wordt geflankeerd door twee volwassen personen in klassieke kledij.

artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 33 cm x width 25 cm × depth 3.7 cm
artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

artworks.medium: metal, organic material, inorganic material, oil (organic material), copper (metal)
artworks.dimensions: height 33.7 cm x width 26.6 cm
artworks.description:
Angels support the dead body of Christ in front of his tomb. In the basket are nails and a crown of thorns: the instruments of his Passion. This small, stirring depiction was intended for private devotion and to arouse compassion as well as hope for redemption after death. Bartholomeus Spranger was one of the most influential artists in Europe in the 16th century and court painter to Emperor Rudolf II in Prague, 
whose exceptional art collection was internationally acclaimed.

artworks.title: Hugo de Groot op jonge leeftijd
artworks.medium: metal, plant material, paint (coating), biological material, inorganic material, oil paint (paint), tin (metal), wood (plant material), gilding (material)
artworks.dimensions: height 13.7 cm x width 10.7 cm x depth 1.6 cm × height 10.2 cm x width 8.6 cm
artworks.description: Hoewel op de achterzijde een kleine sticker met de naam Henri IV is aangebracht, betreft het hier een buste van Hugo de Groot als 15-jarige jongeman. Hij is van rechts in driekwartprofiel gezien en gezeten met zijn rechterhand in de zij, de elleboog naar de beschouwer gedraaid. Het wonderkind Hugo de Groot had in 1599 al een universitaire studie achter de rug: tijdens zijn verblijf in Frankrijk in 1598 was hij in de rechten gepromoveerd. Koning Hendrik IV schonk hem bij deze gelegenheid een medaillon met een portret van de koning zelf, dat De Groot hier in de linkerhand houdt. Dit medaillon heeft waarschijnlijk aanleiding gegeven tot de verkeerde identificatie. De identificatie als Hugo de Groot op jongere leeftijd is gebaseerd op een portretgravure van Jacob de Gheyn (II) uit 1599, zie collectie Rijksmuseum, RP-P-OB-9953 en op het feit dat in vroege beschrijvingen van het Panpoëticon Batavum sprake is van een portret van Hugo de Groot op jonge leeftijd.

artworks.title: Ceiling with representations of Morning and Evening
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 170 cm x width 499 cm × height 305 cm x width 506 cm
artworks.description: Ceiling from the bedroom of Mary Stuart, painted by T. C. van der Schuer, 1678. The wooden ceiling is from the bedchamber of Mary Stuart, wife of Prince William III. The room was at the stadholder's residence in the Binnenhof in The Hague. In 1672 William and Mary had the stadholder's quarters refurbished. Mary would have seen the ceiling as she rose and retired to bed. Which is why it is decorated with mythological scenes reflecting the themes of dawn and night. The two main scenes are on canvas. In the first the goddess Aurora chases the darkness with her torch, flying ahead of the sun god Apollo. On the other side of the ceiling night approaches and Apollo is chased away by a female figure.

artworks.title: Portrait of Hendrik Brouwer, Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 33 cm x width 25 cm × depth 3.5 cm
artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

Pieter Both, 1610-1614
Gerard Reynst, 1614-1615
Laurens Reael,1615-1619
Jan Pietersz Coen, 1619-1623 and 1627-1629
Pieter de Carpentier, 1623-1627

Joan Maetsuycker, 1653-1678

artworks.artist: workshop of Jan Antonisz van Ravesteyn

artworks.description: These portraits were originally displayed at Honselaarsdijk, the palace built by Stadholder Frederick Henry and his wife Amalia in the 1620s near The Hague. In the style of European courts of the day, one of the palace rooms was lined with portraits of ancestors, relatives and celebrities past and present. Many of these personalities played a role in the Eighty Years War: members of the Nassau family and other commanders of the Dutch Republic's army, officers of the French and English allies and leading Spanish generals. A remarkable aspect is the number of foreigners who fought for the Dutch. The Republic's army enjoyed an international reputation and attracted young noblemen from abroad. For them, the war was a career opportunity.

He imported slaves to New Netherland from West Africa. Steendam is better known for his poetry. It was in New Netherland that he wrote his Prickelvaersen encouraging the foundation of a colony on the Delaware river.

artworks.title: Portrait of Viglius ab Zuichemus, Frisian Jurist, President of the Privy Council and Member of the Council of State
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 46 cm x width 35.3 cm x thickness 1.2 cm × depth 5.5 cm
artworks.description:
Viglius van Aytta van Zwichem, 1507-1577, humanist, jurist, staatsman, geestelijke. Door een onbekende Zuidnederlandse schilder.
Viglius (latijn voor het Friese Wigle) voerde als devies: 'Vita mortalium vigilia' dat is 'Het leven der stervelingen is waken'. Een opsomming van zijn aktiviteiten toont dat hij zijn devies heeft waargemaakt: archivaris en bibliothecaris der Bourgondische vorsten; proost van het kapittel van Sint Bavo, Gent; hoogleraar in de rechten, rechter in de hoogste colleges als het Rijkskamergerecht te Spiers en de Grote Raad te Mechelen. Verder vervulde hij vele politieke functies, waarvan de voornaamste lid van de Consulta of Achterraad, die landvoogdes Margaretha van Parma adviseerde. Na de afstand van Karel V werd Viglius enerzijds verdacht van sympathie voor de hervorming, anderzijds van te grote meegaandheid met het Spaanse bestuur.

artworks.title: Portrait of Rycklof van Goens, Governor-General of the Dutch East India Company
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 33 cm x width 25 cm × depth 3.5 cm
artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

Pieter Both, 1610-1614
Gerard Reynst, 1614-1615
Laurens Reael,1615-1619
Jan Pietersz Coen, 1619-1623 and 1627-1629
Pieter de Carpentier, 1623-1627
Jacques Specx, 1629-1632
Hendrick Brouwer, 1632-1636

Cornelis van der Lijn, 1645-1650

Joan Maetsuycker, 1653-1678
Rycklof van Goens, 1678-1681
Cornelis Speelman, 1681-1684
