artworks.title: Achterkant van het schilderij met het portret van Rutger Jan Schimmelpenninck (1761-1825)
artworks.medium: plant material, biological material, wood (plant material), paper, panel
artworks.dimensions: height 45.5 cm x width 37.2 cm x depth 0.7 cm
artworks.description: Rutger Jan Schimmelpenninck, by C. Hodges, 1805. Rutger Jan Schimmelpenninck (1761-1825) had been a Patriot from the very start. In 1796 he was elected to the National Assembly of the Batavian Republic. From 1798 he served the Republic as its representative in Paris and London. On the recommendation of France's Emperor Napoleon, in 1805, Schimmelpenninck was appointed grand pensionary. As such, he led the Batavian Republic from April 1805 to June 1806. In that short period a number of significant reforms were achieved in the fields of education and taxation. But under pressure from Napoleon, Schimmelpenninck was eventually forced to resign from office.

artworks.title: Hendrik Swaardecroon (1667-1728). Gouverneur-generaal (1718-25)
artworks.artist: copy after Hendrik van den Bosch
artworks.medium: metal, paint (coating), inorganic material, copper (metal), oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: depth 3.7 cm × height 33.5 cm x width 26 cm
artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

Pieter Both, 1610-1614
Gerard Reynst, 1614-1615
Laurens Reael,1615-1619
Jan Pietersz Coen, 1619-1623 and 1627-1629
Pieter de Carpentier, 1623-1627

Cornelis van der Lijn, 1645-1650
Karel Reiniersz, 1650-1653
Joan Maetsuycker, 1653-1678
Rycklof van Goens, 1678-1681
Cornelis Speelman, 1681-1684

Abraham van Riebeeck, 1709-1713

artworks.description: The highest-ranking Dutch East India Company (VOC) official in Asia was the governor-general. He presided in the Castle of Batavia (now Jakarta, Indonesia), a fort built by the Dutch. The assembly hall in the Castle of Batavia was the centre of Dutch power in Asia. artworks.title: Portrait of Joan Maetsuyker, Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 33 cm x width 25 cm × depth 3.5 cm
artworks.description:
Portraits of the governors general. At the head of the VOC administration in Asia was the governor general, the chairman of the East Indies Council, which met in Batavia. The Council's assembly chamber at the Castle in Batavia was the focal point of Dutch power. Along the walls hung the portraits of all the past governors general, symbolising the continuity of the Dutch presence. Smaller copies at the Company's offices in the Netherlands represented the VOC's power in Asia. The copies displayed here probably come from the VOC's Rotterdam Chamber. Some of the portraits from the series that hung in Batavia are displayed above in the VOC gallery that circles this room.

artworks.description: Drieluik met de steniging van Stephanus en de legende van het vinden van zijn graf (in de originele architectonische lijst, en met vaste vleugels). Op het middenpaneel het martelaarschap van de heilige Stephanus die door een woedende menigte wordt gestenigd. Op de voorgrond legt een man zijn mantel aan de voeten van Saulus. In de hemel de verschijning van Chriustus en God de Vader. In de verte wordt het lichaam van de heilige begraven. Rechts het visioen van de priester Lucianus waarin Gamaliël aan zijn bed verschijnt en hem vertelt waar hij het graf met de overblijfselen van de heilige kan vinden. Op het linker zijpaneel verschijnt Christus als tuinman aan Maria Magdalena, Noli me tangere. Op de achtergrond de kruisberg en de heilige vrouwen op weg naar het graf. Op het rechter zijpaneel scènes uit het leven van de heilige Maria Aegyptiaca die in de woestijn de communie ontvangt van de kluizenaar Zosimus, op de achtergrond steekt zij de Jordaan over, en voorstellingen van haar begrafenis en hemelvaart.

artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, panel, oil paint (paint)

artworks.description: In the earliest known Dutch militia portrait, no fewer than seventeen men gaze at us with pride, including, at the upper right, the painter himself holding a paintbrush. The man fourth from the right in the bottom row is probably the captain. The militias were responsible for urban order, public safety and the defence of the city. This group portrait is a textbook example of bourgeois self-awareness and confidence, and typically Dutch.

artworks.description: Venus, the goddess of love, had an affair with the god of war, Mars. artworks.description: The young, beardless Samson ripped a ferocious lion apart with just his bare hands. In Heemskerck’s time, this story was regarded as the forerunner (prefiguration) of Christ’s victory over the devil. Pluto, recognizable by his three-headed dog Cerberus, was the guardian of the underworld in classical mythology. In the 16th century he was also identified with the devil from Christianity.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 73 cm x width 60 cm
artworks.description:
The Dutch landscape painter Hendrik Voogd had a successful career in Italy. During a visit to his homeland, he was portrayed by the celebrated English portraitist Charles Howard Hodges, who worked in the Netherlands. Hodges must have been honoured by the commission and portrayed Voogd not as an artist, but as a gentleman. The distinguished demeanour and serious gaze confirm Voogd’s established position 
as an artist.

artworks.description: The French diplomat, soldier, and spy Chevalier(ère) d’Éon (1728–1810) lived 50 years as a man and then 30 years as a woman, becoming a celebrity at the time. In this portrait, d’Éon presents as a woman and supporter of the French revolution, including a cockade on her hat. D’Éon is one of the few historical figures known to have lived beyond traditional gender boundaries.

artworks.title: The Siege of Schenkenschans in 1636
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: support: height 55.4 cm x width 141.7 cm x thickness 6 cm
artworks.description: Thirteen paintings once hung in a gallery glorifying Frederick Henry’s military triumphs. This is the only one that has been preserved: it depicts his victory on 29 April 1636 at Schenkenschans, on the Republic’s eastern border where the rivers Rhine and Waal split. Whoever controls this stronghold, controls access to the country. While Schenkenschans is being attacked from the rivers, a fierce battle between a combined Dutch-French army and Spanish forces is raging in the foreground.

This painting reflects his experimentation with their bright vibrant colours, short brushstrokes, and modern compositions. The scene is a close-up of a bank of the Seine River near Asnières, a town northeast of Paris. Van Gogh enjoyed painting there during the summer of 1887.

artworks.description: At the age of 18, Bep Rietveld painted this self-portrait as a learning assignment under the guidance of the painter Charley Toorop. The fluent contour of her head and shoulders, the stylized facial features, and slightly enlarged eyes create a penetrating portrait. Rietveld met Toorop through her father, the architect Gerrit Rietveld, and learned from her to ‘observe the way she did.’

artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, oil paint (paint), panel
artworks.dimensions: height 20.8 cm x width 16.7 cm
artworks.description: Like his forefathers, Jan van der Pluym, here aged 69, was a prosperous slater and plumber in Leiden. Upon his death, he left behind 15 residential houses and to each of his four children 16,000 guilders. These portraits are the smallest Rembrandt ever painted. In contrast to his more formal commissions from strangers, the execution of these family likenesses is very free and sketchy. The artist may have made them as a personal favour.

artworks.title: Pietje (Girl Reading)
artworks.medium: metal, wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), gold (metal), precious metal, biological material, inorganic material, oil paint (paint), gold leaf, panel
artworks.dimensions: height 42 cm x width 32 cm
artworks.description:
Pietje was probably a relative of Suze Robertson’s childminder. The artist painted her in this pose at least three times. In this version, the gold leaf behind her head forms a striking contrast to the painted brown tones. Robertson was fascinated by gold, initially
rendering it in paint. Here she boldly took this a step further by applying gold leaf. By using this material the painting acquires a mystical aura.

artworks.title: Two Children with a Cat
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 61 cm x width 52 cm
artworks.description: What fun! The boy in colourful attire abruptly snatches a treat from under the cat’s nose. At the same time, he keeps the animal away from the grabbing hands of the other child. The cat seems afraid of the little boy and might lash out unexpectedly. And then, it would become a mix of laughter and tears. Judith Leyster’s loose painting style contributes to the vivacity.

artworks.title: July (‘Summer Luxuriance’)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 120 cm x width 170 cm
artworks.description: It seems as if Van Looy has lavishly strewn blue flowers all over this large canvas. Looking a bit longer, however, one notices the artist’s house in Soest and the hay wagons behind the tall hedge, and in the right foreground an overturned pot among the flowers. The painter was clearly inspired by the landscapes of Van Gogh, but his representation of nature and the fall of light are more realistic.

artworks.description: Even though owls are night predators, this eagle-owl has managed to catch a chicken during the day. It looks up angrily from his prey while being harassed by a wood pigeon. In general, in daytime, other birds ill try to keep owls from sleeping and chase them away. Eagle-owls are rarely found in the Netherlands. Dirk Valkenburg also worked in Vienna, which is where he most likely portrayed this imposing creature.

artworks.title: Burial in My Own Neighbourhood
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 45.8 cm x width 32 cm
artworks.description: A funeral is in progress in the courtyard of the convent in Saint-Germain-en-Laye, France, the painter’s home town. The mournful atmosphere is heightened by the fallow, reddish-brown fields stretching out behind the building. Visible in the distance, against a backdrop of dark hills, is a steam train chugging along, releasing billows of aqua blue smoke. Denis built up his landscape by juxtaposing pure, unmixed colours separated by dark lines.

artworks.title: A town square with a fair
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, hardwood, biological material, oak (wood), paint (coating), panel
artworks.dimensions: height 47 cm x width 59 cm
artworks.description: Een kermis of (jaar-)markt op een groot plein in grootstedelijke omgeving, met centraal een tweetal grote kramen/tijdelijke gebouwen waar het publiek ter lering en/of vermaak op het podium van de linker kraam een gezelschap 'exotisch' geklede personen wordt getoond, waaronder centraal een vrouw, op de achtergrond een zwarte man of black face, een harlekijnachtig personage en een viertal uniform bont geklede personen. Tegen de voorgevel van de kraam een plakkaat/rolschildering met een paard waarop een staande/balancerende vrouw en op de rechter kraam rolschilderingen die tonen wat binnen is te zien: een panter/tijger, een groep apen in een boom, andere dieren en een groep Zuid-Amerikaanse personages, mogelijk marrons. De geografische setting kan niet worden geduid en is vrij zeker een gefantaseerde setting waar wel bestaande gebouwen, waaronder het stadskasteel aan de Neude te Utrecht, is te zien.

artworks.title: Johan François Adriaan Cateau van Rosevelt (1823-91). Chef van het Bouwdepartement en Agent-generaal van de Immigratie in Suriname
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 135 cm x width 93 cm × depth 14 cm
artworks.description: Johan F.A. Cateau van Rosevelt by Lovera, 1885. Cateau van Rosevelt (1823-1891) was chief officer at the Surinamese immigration department. After the abolition of slavery in 1863, contract workers, or coolies, were recruited in India and Java. By 1900 the Hindus and Javanese had combined with the originally European and African population and the native Indians to form a pluriform but segregated society in Surinam. On his lap, Cateau - 'coolie papa' - has a map of Surinam, which was made under his direction.

artworks.title: Portrait of Joseph-Charles de Meulemeester in the Loggia of the Vatican
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, oil paint (paint), canvas
artworks.dimensions: height 75.5 cm x width 57.4 cm
artworks.description:
The painters Ducq and De Meulemeester belonged to the Southern Netherlandish artists-in-training who were sent by the government to Rome to study Italian masterpieces. In a passage of the Vatican decorated by the renowned painter Raphael, De Meulemeester shows us his copy of the ceiling painting above him. His aim was to reproduce all of Raphael’s work. On the chair is his palette, watercolour box, and brush
in a glass of water.

artworks.title: Vanitas stilleven

artworks.dimensions: height 78.6 cm x width 103.5 cm
artworks.description: Op een stenen tafel staat in het midden een vaas met bloemen, daarom heen is een groot aantal objecten geplaatst. Links staat een kistje dat voornamelijk met gouden munten is gevuld, daarnaast ligt een ratelaar, een medaillon, twee sinaasappels, een takje met rozen, een doodshoofd met een bloemenkrans, een boek, een horloge, de twee stenen tafelen met de tien geboden en een zonnebloem. Voorop ligt nog een blad papier waarop de geschilderde objecten worden genoemd met daarachter een verwijzing naar een Bijbeltekst. Links op de achtergrond is een getralied raam zichtbaar.

Ewer and basin. Silver gilt. Paris, c. 1809, by Abel-Etienne Giroux. Dressing table. Oak, veneered with mahogany, gilt bronze mounts. Amsterdam, 1809, by Carel Breytspraak. Made for the bedchamber of Prince Napoleon Louis, the son of King Louis Napoleon, in the Royal Palace on Dam Square in Amsterdam. On loan from H.M. the Queen, Royal Palace, Amsterdam.

A bust of the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius bears witness to their interest in antiquity, while paintings by Jacob de Wit (1695-1754) on the easel and on the wall bespeak their love of art.

artworks.title: Portrait of Jaapgen Caerlsdr
artworks.medium: wood (plant material), plant material, paint (coating), biological material, oil paint (paint), panel
artworks.dimensions: height 19.9 cm x width 16.7 cm
artworks.description: Jaapgen Caerlsdr is 70 years old in this portrait. Hailing from a distinguished lineage, she was the daughter of a Leiden glazier. She probably sat for Rembrandt around 27 March 1635, when she served as a witness at her granddaughter’s baptism in Amsterdam. The diagonal placement of her upper body and the subtle use of shadows, for instance in the fold of the cap, contribute to her lifelike, almost three-dimensional appearance.

artworks.title: De heilige Alexis
artworks.medium: paint (coating), textile materials, canvas, oil paint (paint)
artworks.dimensions: height 130 cm x width 170 cm
artworks.description: De heilige Alexis ligt languit uitgestrekt met zijn ogen opwaarts gericht. Hij ligt op een gevlochten mat waarop een bedelaarsstaf en -nap liggen. Hij is omwikkeld door een rood kleed, die zijn schouders en linkerarm onbedekt laat. In zijn rechterhand omklemt hij een stukje papier. Zijn andere hand raakt met enkele vingers een houten kruis dat op de mat ligt. In de lucht zweven twee engelen en daarnaast engelenkopjes met vleugels. De heilige lijkt zijn (laatste) blik te werpen op het gele licht dat midden boven te zien is. De architectuur aan de rechterzijde geeft schematisch een trap aan en verwijst naar de ruimte onder de trap waar de heilige volgens de legende verbleef.
